articles.title: Takaichi faces rule-of-law scrutiny over US sanctions on ICC
articles.summary: TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is under scrutiny regarding the country's commitment to the rule of law following U.S. sanctions against International Criminal Court…

blocks.text: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi enters the prime minister's office in Tokyo on Friday, Aug. 28.

TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is under scrutiny regarding the country's commitment to the rule of law following U.S. sanctions against International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane, the first Japanese to lead the organization.
Initially, Takaichi merely said that the U.S. sanctions against Akane were "very regrettable." This led to criticism as the remark was perceived as a weak response.
The focus is on whether Japan can dissuade the United States from seeking to "dismantle" the ICC.
On Tuesday, Takaichi told reporters that the U.S. sanctions were "incompatible with the Japanese position and we take them seriously."
"We must protect Ms. Akane and the precious organization of the ICC as the largest contributor to it," the prime minister also said.

Japan values the rule of law and has consistently supported the ICC. The government is on high alert for further U.S. sanctions. If the ICC itself becomes a target, its operations could be severely affected.
"The sanctions against the ICC are a crisis of the rule of law," Akane said at a press conference Wednesday.
She urged the Japanese government to make "maximum efforts," including by engaging with the United States. The government plans to respond in close cooperation with Akane.
On Friday, Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi held a telephone conversation with Akane to discuss the situation surrounding the ICC.
However, it remains unclear how assertive Japan can be as the country has made its alliance with the United States the cornerstone of its diplomacy and security policy.
The government has not protested or called for a withdrawal regarding the latest sanctions, which have drawn criticism even from the ruling Liberal Democratic Party.
"We are engaging with the United States while saying what needs to be said," Motegi told a press conference Friday.
However, a government official said, "We can't be too tough on the United States."
Under the banner of the rule of law, the Takaichi administration has criticized China and Russia for attempting to change the status quo by force.

If Japan turns a blind eye to threats to the rule of law out of consideration for the United States, its credibility could be significantly undermined. Public opinion is also scrutinizing the government's handling of the issue.

"The prime minister's initial remarks drew various criticisms," a government official said, expressing concerns that any further impact on the Takaichi administration's approval ratings would be damaging.

articles.title: Norway's new king pays tribute to his late father as tens of thousands mourn
articles.summary: OSLO, Norway (AP) — King Haakon VIII of Norway used his first speech in his new role to eulogize his father, King Harald V, as a loving parent and dedicated monarch a day after he died at 89. “We are…

blocks.text: Norway's King Haakon at the palace in Oslo, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026. (Heiko Junge, Pool Photo via AP)
OSLO, Norway (AP) — King Haakon VIII of Norway used his first speech in his new role to eulogize his father, King Harald V, as a loving parent and dedicated monarch a day after he died at 89.

“We are in mourning. At the same time, it brings us comfort and strength to know that so many are mourning with us,” the king said wearing a black suit as his speech was shown live on public television.
After Harald V’s death on Friday morning, the crown prince became King Haakon VIII immediately.
He thanked the people for their outpouring of compassion and remembered what a loving father and husband Harald had been.
Tens of thousands of mourners paid their respects, placing flowers and condolence cards outside the royal palace in Oslo, where the coffin arrived late Friday from the hospital.
Across the country, churches and city halls opened specially so people could light candles, and write their thoughts about the deceased king in condolence books.

“It has been a powerful and moving experience to see the Palace Square filled with people, flowers, messages of condolence, and candles. Thank you so much,” 53-year-old Haakon said, sitting on a wooden desk next to his father's portrait and two white candles.

“As king, my father represented Norway and the Norwegian people with pride and joy, through visits around the country, at events here at the royal palace, and while working on Norway’s behalf around the world,” Haakon said.

“I’m going to miss him. I’ll miss his laughter. His good-natured way of dealing with people and situations,” he added, trying to hold back his tears as he vowed to give everything for the country in the future as its new king.
“And that means — in the ultimate sense — being willing to risk everything, even one’s life, for Norway’s freedom and independence.”

Haakon adopted the motto “All for Norway,” which dates back to his great-grandfather. His wife became Queen Mette-Marit, while his oldest child, Ingrid Alexandra, became crown princess and heir to the throne.

Earlier on Saturday, the new king and Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra welcomed Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and the presiding bishop of the Lutheran Church of Norway to the palace where King Harald's coffin was lying in state, the royal palace said in a statement.
On Sunday morning, the Church of Norway is holding memorial services across the country, with the royal family expected to attend the service at Asker Church, southwest of Oslo, the palace said.
Haakon is well acquainted with his royal obligations. As his father aged and his health declined in recent years, Haakon stepped in as regent on several occasions.

His tasks in the near future will include shoring up support for the monarchy following controversies over his wife’s past contacts with deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and his stepson’s rape conviction.

A date for the funeral has not been set, but the country is officially in a state of mourning and some people decided to postpone celebrations such as weddings and baptisms until after the mourning period has passed, Norwegian public broadcaster NRK reported.

Norway’s monarchy has old roots, tracing its origins to King Harald Fairhair in the ninth century. When Norway regained its independence from Sweden in 1905, three-quarters of voters in a national plebiscite approved restoring the monarchy.
Today, the role is largely symbolic as power lies with an elected parliament, but the royal family retains celebrity and a role in promoting the wealthy nation around the world.

articles.title: 106 barangays in Cordillera warned of landslides due to continuous rains
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY -- The Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) Cordillera warned 106 barangays located in landslide-prone areas that they could be potentially affected by landslides due to the incessant rains…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY -- The Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) Cordillera warned 106 barangays located in landslide-prone areas that they could be potentially affected by landslides due to the incessant rains experienced by the southwest monsoon or "habagat".

The agency said that Benguet province has 24 landslide-prone areas in the towns of Atok, Bokod, Itogon, La Trinidad, and Tublay, including Baguio City, while Kalinga has the largest concentration with 50 areas in Tabuk City, Pinukpuk, and Rizal, particularly barangay Liwan.

In Ifugao, there are 22 high-risk areas in the towns of Aguinaldo and Alfonso Lista, while in the town of Paracelis, there are seven barangays in Mountain Province and three barangays in Conner, Apayao.

The MGB said that the two barangays are both located in mountainous areas, and with the continuous rains experienced by the region for a month and with the continued rains in September, the risk of sudden landslides is high.

In PAGASA's August 30, 2-26 Weather Advisory No.30, the province of Benguet, including Baguio City, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac, and Pampanga, will experience Orange Rainfall from 100-200 mm, while some parts of the Cordillera will experience 5-100 mm rainfall.

The MGB-Cordillera called on provincial, city, and municipal governments and councils to strictly monitor landslide-prone areas and conduct forced evacuation of residents living in mountainous areas threatened by landslides.

articles.title: PC Andrew Harper’s killers will remain in jail as PM makes changes to early release scheme
articles.summary:
Andy Burnham says ‘hundreds’ of people will remain in prison as part of changes to scheme designed to ease overcrowding

PC Andrew Harper’s killers will be excluded from the early release…

blocks.text: PC Andrew Harper’s killers will be excluded from the early release scheme after the prime minister said anyone convicted of unlawful killing would be exempt.
Andy Burnham said “hundreds” of people will remain in prison as part of changes to the scheme designed to ease overcrowding in prisons.

“We’ve come up with a proposal which will allow not just those guilty of manslaughter, the people involved in the killing of PC Harper, but those who have been convicted for indecent assault, those convicted for death by dangerous driving, all of these offenders now will remain in prison. Hundreds of them,” the prime minister told the BBC.
“I heard obviously what Andrew Harper’s family were saying. I mean who couldn’t? Nobody would want a position to arise where those guilty of killing a police officer are let out early from prison.”
Burnham said extra space in prisons would be created by deporting foreign prisoners and releasing some prisoners who are serving indefinite sentences.
The prime minister ordered a review of the scheme, which is being undertaken by the justice secretary, Alex Norris, and is set to be published when parliament returns from summer recess in September.
That followed widespread condemnation of the scheme when it emerged that Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole could be released halfway through their 13-year sentences.
In August 2019, Harper, 28, died when he was dragged down a country road in Berkshire by a car as Cole, Bowers and their accomplice Henry Long fled the scene of a quad bike theft.

All three were convicted of manslaughter in 2020. Cole and Bowers were sentenced to 13 years in prison and could have potentially been released early as part of the government’s drive to free up prison places.

articles.title: One Nation’s Secret Harbour byelection win shows Labor is at a loss when it comes to calming angry voters | Analysis
articles.summary:
Even after a week in which Pauline Hanson and One Nation candidates tripped over themselves trying to explain key policies, voters still backed the party

The One Nation hype machine went…

blocks.text: The One Nation hype machine went into overdrive after Saturday’s Secret Harbour byelection but one thing is clear from the thumping victory.

Despite the party’s sustained surge in public support, Labor and the Coalition still don’t have any idea how to calm an angry electorate and dint support for Pauline Hanson and her insurgent movement.

Even before One Nation’s Luke Herdegen was confirmed as having easily defeated Labor’s Georgia Tree in the suburban Western Australia seat previously held by Labor, One Nation’s WA leader Rod Caddies declared there were “no safe Labor seats in this state or in this country any more”.
By Sunday morning, Nationals defector Barnaby Joyce said “politics has changed” in favour of One Nation, even claiming the polls were underplaying One Nation’s support nationally.

The party was on track for a swing towards it of more than 20% against Labor in the beachside electorate, a result Hanson said revealed deep seated and growing anger towards Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and the federal Labor government.

Although it is easy to overstate single byelection results, when voter behaviour is often quite different from general elections, the win shows under the right conditions, Hanson has the capacity to take seats from Labor, as well as the Liberals and Nationals.

Unless there is a significant shift between now and the next federal election, due in early 2028, incumbent MPs from all sides should fear One Nation and a voting electorate that appears increasingly ready to burn the whole show down.

It has mattered little that Hanson and her motley crew in Canberra had a terrible week, tripping over themselves seemingly every day trying to explain One Nation’s immigration policy, the key issue for the party’s base.

Since Farrer MP David Farley failed to explain where cuts to lower net overseas migration would come from on TV last Sunday, Hanson and Joyce have both repeatedly flubbed their explanation of what Farley had actually meant to say. One Nation’s strategist James Ashby even appeared on News 24 after dark with a mop, admitting a clean up job was required.
Taking in part of Perth’s southern coastal suburbs, Secret Harbour sits almost entirely within the federal electorate of Canning, held by Liberal frontbencher Andrew Hastie.

Hanson, her billionaire benefactor and many One Nation supporters hold a special dislike for Hastie, because he gave evidence against accused war criminal and Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith. But Hastie was right in criticising the Liberal campaign under state leader and former television host Basil Zempilas.
after newsletter promotion

Lackluster opposition to One Nation, in the misguided belief that any loss for Labor was a win for the Liberals, has left Zempilas and his diminished party wanting on Sunday. The best defence he could offer before the loss was to complain that the Liberals would have fared better in a byelection held in a seat closer to the Perth CBD.

Hastie’s message is right. Only a strong, values-led fightback against Hanson, including linking her to US President Donald Trump, is the way to fightback. Wishy washy answers about preference deals and hypothetical minority government arrangements is misguided. Opposition leader Angus Taylor should take note.

On Sunday, Albanese told the Labor faithful in Queensland the the party owed it to history to defeat Hanson’s dangerous, divisive, dishonest politics. Fighting back on hip pocket issues still remains Labor’s best chance of stopping Hanson winning enough seats to really change things in Canberra.
The next federal election is more than a year away, but the Secret Harbour result is the latest evidence in the failure of the major parties to effectively put One Nation back in its box.

articles.title: CHR urges stronger safeguards for journalists on Press Freedom Day
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Marking National Press Freedom Day, the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) called for stronger safeguards for journalists, citing the country’s 114th place in Reporters Without…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Marking National Press Freedom Day, the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) called for stronger safeguards for journalists, citing the country’s 114th place in Reporters Without Borders’ 2026 World Press Freedom Index.
In a statement on Sunday, the CHR warned that press freedom in the Philippines continues to “face serious challenges.”
In April, Reporters Without Borders said the Philippines improved from 116th last year but remains in the lower half of its 180-country press freedom index.

“The lack of accountability for crimes against media workers perpetuates a dangerous cycle of impunity,” said the CHR as the agency urged the government to ensure swift justice for victims and their families.
The CHR also said red-tagging, vilification and other forms of intimidation likewise pose threats to journalists and the public’s right to information.
The CHR cited its National Inquiry on Red-tagging, which found journalists were frequently targeted for critical reporting on government policies and programs.
The commission reiterated its recommendation for legislation that would specifically penalize Red-tagging.
As the country’s national human rights institution, the CHR said it continues to strengthen mechanisms aimed at protecting media workers.
Its partnership with the Presidential Task Force on Media Security supports information-sharing, case development and assistance for journalists affected by threats or attacks.
Through CHR’s Alisto! Alert Mechanism, media workers can directly report threats and incidents for monitoring, investigation, and appropriate action.
“Beyond protection mechanisms, laws and policies must foster an environment where journalism can flourish without fear of criminalization or undue restriction,” said the CHR.
The CHR renewed its call to decriminalize libel and cyberlibel, saying journalists should be able to work freely without facing criminal prosecution or undue restrictions.
The commission also urged lawmakers to ensure anti-disinformation efforts do not infringe on constitutional rights.
The CHR also warned of artificial intelligence and digital technologies used to surveil journalists, expose sources, suppress dissent, and spread disinformation.
The CHR urged the government to address impunity and create a safe civic environment free from censorship, intimidation, and other threats.
“When journalists are silenced, people lose information necessary to make informed decisions, participate meaningfully in public life, and hold institutions accountable,” said the CHR. /das

articles.title: Body of missing pregnant Aeta found after 4-day search in Zambales lake
articles.summary: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — The body of a pregnant Aeta woman who had been missing since a boat capsized in Mapanuepe Lake in San Marcelino, Zambales, was recovered Sunday, Aug. 30, four days after the…

blocks.text: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — The body of a pregnant Aeta woman who had been missing since a boat capsized in Mapanuepe Lake in San Marcelino, Zambales, was recovered Sunday, Aug. 30, four days after the incident.
The Philippine Coast Guard confirmed that the body of 26-year-old Arryn Paanan Liwanag was recovered at 11:20 a.m., bringing the death toll to nine.
Liwanag was the last of three people who remained missing after the boat carrying 13 Aetas capsized near the Sunken Church in Barangay Buhawen on Aug. 27.
The bodies of the other two missing passengers, Chandnea Serrano Dela Cruz, 3, and Anqelito Serrano Liwanag, 8, were recovered on Saturday.

The other fatalities were identified as Elvis Tiglao Pabalan, 33; Joanavie Mae Tiglao Pabalan; Sally Serrano Dela Cruz, 29; Prince Lenard Serrano Dela Cruz, 1; Evelyn Yurik Lagman, 45; and Cedric Serrano Liwanag, 2. Four others survived.
The 13 Aetas were from a community in Sitio Lumibao, located across Mapanuepe Lake from the main part of Barangay Buhawen. Residents have to cross the lake by boat to reach the village proper.
The group had gone to Barangay Buhawen for a vaccination program and a 4Ps meeting and was returning to Sitio Lumibao when the boat encountered strong winds and rough waters and capsized.
Search and rescue operations continued for four days, with responders repeatedly suspending the operation because of unfavorable weather conditions.
With Liwanag’s recovery, all 13 people aboard the boat have now been accounted for—nine dead and four survivors. /atm

articles.title: Russian-American heads Trump’s planned Caucasus trade route
articles.summary: Until recently, few people in the South Caucasus had heard of Konstantin Sokolov. Now the 52-year-old Russian-American businessman is at the center of new investment fund backed by US President…

blocks.text: Until recently, few people in the South Caucasus had heard of Konstantin Sokolov. Now the 52-year-old Russian-American businessman is at the center of new investment fund backed by US President Donald Trump.

In mid-July, Sokolov — who emigrated from Russia to the US at age 21 and later founded the investment firm IJS Investments in Chicago — was appointed to head a new investment fund of the US State Department.

The TRIPP+ EnterpriseFund, registered in the US as the Trans-Caspian Enterprise Fund and launched with more than $200 million (about €172.5 million) in capital, is expected to invest in countries across the South Caucasus and Central Asia and help finance the large-scale TRIPP infrastructure project, also known as the “Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity.”

The “Trump Route” is a transit corridor that aims to connect Azerbaijan with its autonomous exclave of Nakhchivan through Armenian territory. The ambitious infrastructure project is part of a peace deal that Armenia and Azerbaijan signed in August 2025 with US mediation. In early June 2026, Washington and Yerevan signed a framework cooperation agreement for the project.
Experts have said construction of the “Trump Route” fits Washington’s strategy of creating a trade corridor between Europe and the region that bypasses existing routes through Russia and Iran.
Sokolov buys up Russian assets in Armenia
Long before he was appointed to head TRIPP+, Sokolov had already established a foothold in Armenia.

In 2024, he acquired Viva Armenia, the country’s largest telecommunications provider. Despite its subsequent partial nationalization, Sokolov continued to expand his holdings. Recently, his companies also bought up the Armenian subsidiary of Russian telecom giant Rostelecom.

blocks.caption: In August 2025, Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev (left) and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan (right) signed a joint declaration ‘peace road map’ after talks with Trump Image: Azerbaijan Presidency/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: An even more significant deal, however, was carried out largely out of the public eye: the purchase of the Teghut copper-molybdenum mine. The mine, which holds an estimated 450 million metric tons of ore and has Armenia’s second-largest reserves, had been taken over by Russia’s state-owned VTB Bank after the company accumulated massive debts. VTB is now under Western sanctions. According to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty’s Armenian service, the deal was carried out through a third-party company.
“Sokolov wanted to avoid a direct deal with the Russian bank,” said Mkrtich Karapetyan, a Radio Liberty journalist who has been investigating the flow of foreign capital into Armenia.
Sokolov: Trump supporter, MAGA backer
While Armenia’s government and its supporters have welcomed the influx of Western capital into the country’s infrastructure projects, the opposition has highlighted serious risks.

Mesrop Manukyan, a lawmaker from the opposition Armenia Alliance, is among Sokolov’s most vocal critics in parliament. He said it’s alarming that a US investor has been able to acquire major stakes in the finance, mining and telecommunications sectors in just a few years.

Manukyan’s faction, which advocates close ties between Armenia and Russia, opposes the TRIPP+ project. It views the “Trump Route” as a disguised “extraterritorial corridor” and the “greatest threat” to Armenia’s security.

Despite his extensive investments, Sokolov remains largely unknown to the Armenian public. There are no official photos of him, and he generally avoids interviews with the local press during business trips.

His most recent visit to the capital, Yerevan, was in early August, when he met with Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan. He was accompanied by Aryeh Lightstone, senior adviser to US special envoy Steve Witkoff.

In Western media, however, Sokolov is known not only for his business ventures in the US and Switzerland but also for his political involvement. Sokolov is a major donor to the US Republican Party and a Trump supporter. According to The Associated Press, he donated about $11 million to Trump’s MAGA movement over the course of a year.
‘Compromise’ between Moscow and Washington?
Benyamin Poghosyan of the Armenian think tank APRI sees two main reasons for Sokolov’s appointment to head the fund.
The first is political. Appointing an American with Russian roots could be “a subtle gesture by Washington aimed at easing Moscow’s fierce criticism of the project,” he told DW.

The second, however, is pragmatic. “Perhaps Russia has nothing to do with it at all. Sokolov may simply have been chosen because he has a deep understanding of the business environment in the former Soviet Union — and because he knows Armenia and how its government works,” said Poghosyan.

blocks.caption: Armenia and Azerbaijan were locked in a conflict over the Nagorno-Karabakh region for decades Image: Tofik Babayev/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: At the same time, the sheer scale of the investment and the financier’s Russian roots are fueling speculation in Armenia. Social media users in the country are debating whether Sokolov, who was born in St. Petersburg, could be a secret “compromise figure” between Moscow and Washington. Supporters of the theory point to the ease with which US companies have acquired formerly Russian assets subject to Western sanctions.

Other observers have refuted the idea, noting that Sokolov has publicly and sharply criticized the Russian government and its war against Ukraine. The funds provided by the US State Department, running through 2036, are seen as flagging Washington’s long-term strategic intentions in the region. During his visit to Yerevan, Aryeh Lightstone told Armenian news outlet CivilNet that the more than $200 million in initial funding could be viewed as a starting point for future investments.

Aram Sargsyan, head of the Republican Party of Armenia and an ally of Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, also rejects the idea that Sokolov is a “compromise figure” for Moscow. He emphasized the practical value of Sokolov’s background, seeing it as an opportunity rather than a cause for concern.
“Sokolov has significant business contacts, understands the Russian mentality perfectly, speaks the language and knows how to work with relevant Russian institutions,” he said. /dl

articles.title: 300 Caraga cops train for BARMM parliamentary polls
articles.summary: CAMP RAFAEL C. RODRIGUEZ, Butuan City – Three hundred policemen of Police Regional Office 13 (PRO 13) have started to undergo a two-day training to serve as members of the PNP Special Electoral Board…

blocks.text: CAMP RAFAEL C. RODRIGUEZ, Butuan City – Three hundred policemen of Police Regional Office 13 (PRO 13) have started to undergo a two-day training to serve as members of the PNP Special Electoral Board (SEB) for the 2026 Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) Parliamentary Election.

The two-day training, which started on Saturday, Aug. 29, was conducted at the PRO13 Multi-Purpose Center here, as part of the preparations to ensure the effective, orderly, and credible conduct of the upcoming parliamentary election.

The training, conducted by the Commission on Elections (Comelec), focused on equipping PNP personnel with the knowledge and practical skills necessary to effectively perform their duties as SEB members.
Topics included the General Instructions for the Electoral Board, particularly the procedures for voting, counting, and transmission of election results.
Participants were also provided with a guide to the Automated Counting Machine Kit, including its proper operation through hands-on exercises.

Regional Public Information Office (RPIO) chief of PRO 13 Police Lt. Col. Jennifer S. Ometer also said the training covered contingency procedures for addressing technical concerns that may arise during the election.
“Kasali sa training ay yun iba pang mga dapat gawin in relation sa BARMM Parliamentary Election,” RPIO chief of PRO 13 added.
Keynote speakers during the training – PRO 13 Director Police Brig. Gen. Rolindo M Suguilon and Caraga Region Comelec Regional Director Attorney Edwin O. Cadungog.

“Let us demonstrate the highest level of discipline and professionalism as we fulfill our mandate in support of the Commission on Elections and our fellow Filipinos during the 2026 BARMM Parliamentary Election,” said Brig. Gen. Suguilon, in his opening remarks.

articles.title: Palace defends Marcos viral video, says ops for calamity response continue
articles.summary: Malacañang on Sunday defended President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. following the circulation of videos showing him singing at First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos" birthday celebration amid the bad…

blocks.text: Published August 30, 2026 1:20pm

Malacañang on Sunday defended President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. following the circulation of videos showing him singing at First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos’ birthday celebration amid the bad weather brought by the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat).

In a statement on Sunday, Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said the President continues to monitor the situation and has ordered concerned agencies to respond accordingly to the impacts of the inclement weather.

“Ang Pangulo ay Pangulo saan man siya naroroon. Ang paglalaan ng ilang oras para sa kanyang pamilya ay hindi nangangahulugang tumitigil ang kanyang tungkulin o ang operasyon ng pamahalaan,” Castro said.
(The President is the President wherever he may be. Spending some time with his family does not mean that he stops performing his duties or that government operations come to a halt.)
“Sa gitna ng matinding pag-ulan, patuloy ang kanyang pagbabantay at pag-uutos sa mga ahensya upang matiyak ang kaligtasan at agarang pagtulong sa ating mga kababayan,” she added.
(Amid the heavy rains, he continues to monitor the situation and direct government agencies to ensure the safety of our people and provide immediate assistance to those affected.)
The First Lady turned 67 on Friday, August 21.
In a separate social media post, the President described the First Lady’s birthday as the “most important day in the calendar.”
“My dear Liza, we're celebrating today a most important day in the calendar; Liza Day!” the President said in a social media post.
“Happy Birthday to the First Lady of every day of my life... and beyond,” he added.
The continuous heavy rains brought by the Habagat caused flooding in Metro Manila and several areas in Luzon on Saturday, August 29.
Among the flooded areas are Dagupan, Pangsinan; Pampanga; Bataan; Bulacan; and Tarlac. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Garcia, Nazario rule WR Bughouse Chess Open
articles.summary: International Master Jan Emmanuel Garcia and National Master Marc Christian Nazario overcame a slow start with a blistering finish in ruling the WR Bughouse Chess Open at the MICE Center in Quezon…

blocks.text: International Master Jan Emmanuel Garcia and National Master Marc Christian Nazario overcame a slow start with a blistering finish in ruling the WR Bughouse Chess Open at the MICE Center in Quezon City over the weekend.

Getting only one-day of practice, Garcia and Nazario, who named their team Bubu Chacha, still came out victorious after edging College of St. Benilde Blazers’ John Laurence Donguines and Daniel Baylosis, 2-1, in their best-of-three title duel to pocket the top purse worth P100,000.

Losing the first match, Garcia, who is part of the team playing in next month’s World Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, and Nazario, who finished in the quarterfinals of the inaugural WR Bughouse Championship last month in Taguig, came roaring back by seizing the next two matches including the rubber.

Metaboys’ Samson Lim III and Jerich Cajeras, who topped the qualification round, swept DCSK’s Noel dela Cruz and Timothy John So Kua in two outings to finish third place in this one-day meet backed by WR Chess’ Wadim Rosenstein, the Philippine Sports Commission, Quezon City and the NCFP.
More than a hundred participants saw action and battled through eight grueling rounds for the eight seats to the playoff stage.

Apart from the four semifinalists, Chronosphere’s IM Pau Bersamina and Rafiel Irvin Lacorte, Datamatics Red’s Mark Kevin Labog and John Michael Magpily, Ruy Lopez Kidz’s Zach Evan Orzame and Marco Piolo Sanido, and Stopper’s IM Michael Concio, Jr. and FIDE Master Alekhine Nouri also made the playoff cut.

articles.title: The president and the penthouse: how Madrid’s government spent €6.3m on a temporary ‘office’
articles.summary:
Saga surrounding purchase for outspoken rightwing regional leader Isabel Díaz Ayuso refuses to go away

The outspoken rightwing leader of the Madrid region is under growing pressure to…

blocks.text: The outspoken rightwing leader of the Madrid region is under growing pressure to explain why her government spent €6.3m (£5.4m) on a residential penthouse purportedly to serve as a temporary workspace while her offices were being renovated.
Isabel Díaz Ayuso, a prominent member of Spain’s opposition conservative People’s party (PP), has been the president of the Madrid region since 2019.

In that time, she has forged a reputation as a politician who prides herself on speaking her mind – and on being a thorn in the side of the country’s socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, whose family and government have been mired in graft allegations for the past two years.

Although Ayuso has frequently accused Sánchez and his Spanish Socialist Workers’ party (PSOE) of being corrupt, she and her administration now face growing calls to provide a transparent explanation for the purchase of the penthouse.

El País reported at the end of July that the Madrid regional government had bought the penthouse in the well-heeled Chamberí neighbourhood of the Spanish capital in April. A spokesperson told the paper the property had been acquired for Ayuso to use while her offices in the Real Casa de Correos – the seat of the regional government – were being renovated. The spokesperson did not respond to questions about the price of the flat, nor whether Ayuso intended to live in it.

It later emerged that the flat cost €6.3m and planning laws meant it could only be used for residential purposes, not as an office. El País reported this week that Ayuso’s government had stipulated that the property it wanted should be “between 250 and 400 square metres and have a large terrace” – the latter being an odd requirement for an office.

blocks.caption: The penthouse flat bought for Ayuso is in the upmarket Chamberí neighbourhood of Madrid.  Photograph: Alessandro Giamello/Alamy

blocks.text: The Madrid president lives with her partner, Alberto González Amador, a businessman who recently put two of the flats they have shared up for sale. González Amador is awaiting trial on charges of tax fraud and falsifying documents. He denies the charges.

Ayuso initially dismissed the revelations as a “smear campaign”, insisting the penthouse was not bought for her to live in but as a venue for “institutional meetings”. She also said she hadn’t had “the faintest idea” about the purchase.
The regional government has subsequently announced that the flat will be sold and the proceeds donated to the victims of this summer’s wildfires near Madrid.

Ayuso recently told reporters she considered the matter closed, saying in her trademark colourful language: “Está en venta, chao pescao”, which roughly translates as: “It’s up for sale, so see you later, alligator”.

The soundbite has elicited comparisons with the time she was caught in congress describing Sánchez as a “hijo de puta” (“son of a bitch”), only to claim she had been misheard and had actually said: “Me gusta la fruta” (“I like fruit”). It has become one of her most well-known pronouncements, along with her electoral slogan of “communism or freedom”.

However, the row over the flat refuses to die down. A judge in Madrid is investigating five separate complaints relating to its purchase and Ayuso’s own boss has said there were still questions to answer. In an interview last week, the PP leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, said that while he was satisfied with her explanations, the relevant department in the regional government “ought to explain why a property that can’t be used as an office was bought”.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the leader of the People’s party, said there were still questions to answer over the matter. Photograph: David Canales/Sopa Images/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Feijóo said Ayuso’s team had told him in April that they were looking for temporary offices. That acknowledgment appears to be at odds with Ayuso’s insistence she was ignorant of the purchase.
Her opponents have seized on the row, with the central government dismissing her explanations as “patently insufficient and patently worrying”, and calling for her to resign.

“So they were looking for ‘temporary offices’ and they got in touch with an estate agent who specialises in luxury properties (not offices) and they requested something that was between 250 square metres and 400 square metres and which had that vital feature any administrative office requires – a big terrace,” said one PSOE councillor in the Madrid town of Móstoles. “See you later, alligator … but with a terrace.”

Pablo Simón, a political scientist at the Carlos III University of Madrid, said the “lack of clear explanations” over the purchase, combined with the judge’s investigation, had left Ayuso in a difficult predicament.
“From a political perspective, I think this has hurt her, because ultimately it’s a very cross-cutting issue that has generated criticism from both the left and the right,” he said.

Simón said while the current “wear and tear” was unlikely to prevent Ayuso winning another term at next year’s regional election, it could result in the loss of her absolute majority and force her to strike a deal with the far-right Vox party to remain in government.

articles.title: Gugu River in Pampanga overflows, breaching Minalin dike
articles.summary: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga, Philippines — Raging waters from the Gugu River breached a portion of the San Fernando-Santo Tomas-Minalin tail dike in Minalin town early Sunday, Aug. 30, sending…

blocks.text: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga, Philippines — Raging waters from the Gugu River breached a portion of the San Fernando-Santo Tomas-Minalin tail dike in Minalin town early Sunday, Aug. 30, sending floodwaters toward an adjacent dike in neighboring Santo Tomas town.
Minalin Mayor Philip Siojo Naguit had been urging residents of villages near the dike to evacuate to safer areas since late Saturday night as water levels continued to rise.
At about dawn on Sunday, a roughly 30-meter portion of the tail dike near Barangay Santa Catalina in Minalin was breached, authorities said.

Pampanga Vice Gov. Dennis Pineda said in a social media post that water from the Gugu River also overflowed into the adjacent San Francisco River, cutting off the road connecting Minalin and Betis in Guagua town.
In Santo Tomas, Mayor John Sambo had appealed to residents living near the tail dike’s checkgate to evacuate late Saturday night and seek shelter in schools with multistory classroom buildings.
Sambo warned that floodwaters flowing from the breached portion in Minalin could reach the checkgate and eventually overtop or breach it, putting nearby communities at risk of flooding.

“Dahil sa lakas ng agos ng tubig sa Gugu River, na-overtop po ang Gugu Dike at pumasok po ang tubig sa ating dike. Malamang na hindi po kakayanin ng ating checkgate ang lahat ng tubig na pumapasok sa ating dike,” he said.
(“Because of the force of the water from Gugu River, it overtopped, and the water spilled over to Gugu Dike. Our checkgate probably can no longer contain all the water entering our dike.
The mayor said the municipal government did not have enough resources to evacuate all residents living near the dike and urged them to voluntarily move to safer areas.
Authorities continued to monitor water levels and the condition of the dikes as heavy rains associated with the enhanced southwest monsoon persisted over Pampanga. /atm

articles.title: E. Samar gov urges stronger LGU-school ties on safety
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY, Philippines — Eastern Samar Gov. Ralph Vincent Evardone has called for stronger cooperation between local governments and the education sector to address school safety concerns and…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY, Philippines — Eastern Samar Gov. Ralph Vincent Evardone has called for stronger cooperation between local governments and the education sector to address school safety concerns and ensure that students receive the support they need to learn and thrive.

Evardone made the call during the Department of Education (DepEd) Eastern Visayas’ 6th Regional Management Committee (Remancom) meeting on Aug. 27 in Borongan City, where education officials assessed the performance, challenges, and support requirements of school divisions across the region.
“It takes a village to raise a child,” Evardone said, noting that protecting students and improving education require the shared responsibility of government, schools, families, and communities.

The push for stronger school safety comes as schools across Eastern Visayas remain on heightened alert following the June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City, where three students were killed, and 20 others were injured.

The incident prompted schools and local governments to review security arrangements and strengthen coordination with law enforcement agencies, particularly in monitoring threats, managing emergencies, and protecting students and school personnel.

Similar security concerns later led to temporary class suspensions in some schools in Eastern Samar and in other parts of the region after online threats were reported. This underscored the need for schools to have clear protocols for threat assessment, emergency response, and coordination with authorities.

Evardone said government support for schools should go beyond infrastructure and educational resources, stressing the importance of creating learning environments where students are protected from threats and other risks.

The incident prompted schools and local governments to review security arrangements and strengthen coordination with law enforcement agencies, particularly in monitoring threats, managing emergencies and protecting students and school personnel.

The developments have also highlighted that school safety is closely linked to learning. Fear, disruptions and insecurity can affect students’ attendance, concentration, and overall well-being, making the involvement of local governments and other community stakeholders essential.

The Remancom meeting also provided an opportunity for DepEd officials and schools division leaders to identify challenges affecting learners and teachers and determine areas where additional intervention or technical assistance may be needed.

Among the concerns discussed were supporting struggling learners, sustaining quality instruction, and strengthening school safety and preparedness. The assessment is expected to help the DepEd regional office tailor its technical assistance to each school division’s specific needs. /atm

articles.title: Serbia keeps EU, Russia in play ahead of key election
articles.summary: Smoke from the wildfires still hangs over parts of Serbia, but as the flames slowly recede another debate is taking shape in their wake — one that has less to do with firefighting and more with…

blocks.text: Smoke from the wildfires still hangs over parts of Serbia, but as the flames slowly recede another debate is taking shape in their wake — one that has less to do with firefighting and more with politics.

In early August, wildfires swept across Serbia, burning through more than 3,500 hectares (8,600 acres) in the Deliblato Sands Special Nature Reserve. Firefighters, soldiers and helicopters battled the flames for days.

Then a Russian Ilyushin Il-76 firefighting aircraft arrived in the southern city of Nis. Serbia had turned to Moscow for help, making Russia the first foreign country it asked to provide a firefighting aircraft. Pro-government media greeted its arrival with celebratory coverage, dubbing the aircraft the “Russian beast.”

“Considering that there are no firefighting aircraft of this capacity available within the European Union, the arriving Russian aircraft will significantly strengthen our capacities to fight the fires,” said Luka Causic, head of the Serbian Interior Ministry’s Department for Emergency Situations.
A pragmatic choice between EU, Russia — or a political signal?
The episode, however, was already being viewed through a geopolitical lens, as Serbia had sought Russian assistance before activating the EU’s emergency mechanism.

When it did call on the EU, the response was swift. Brussels mobilized four helicopters from its strategic rescEU reserve, based in Czechia, Romania and Slovakia, along with ground firefighting teams from Germany and Romania.

blocks.caption: Emergency services, including German firefighters, were on hand to help Serbia battle wildfires Image: Feuerwehr Bonn/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: President Aleksandar Vucic rejected the idea that turning to Russia first was a foreign-policy decision or a sign of Serbia’s political alignment with Moscow.

“As far as equipment and resources are concerned, we are a European giant. The helicopters we received from Europe to fight the fires are less capable than ours and have a lower carrying capacity than our own,” Vucic said during a visit to the Deliblato Sands.
Zelenskyy in Belgrade
The wildfire episode came less than two weeks after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made his first official visit to Serbia.

The two presidents reaffirmed their support for each other’s territorial integrity, which is particularly significant for Belgrade because Ukraine does not recognize the independence of Kosovo . Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008, which Belgrade still does not recognize.
But Vucic is also trying to keep the other side on board, said Vuk Vuksanovic, a political scientist and foreign policy lecturer at King’s College London.

Vuksanovic argues that Vucic’s engagement with Zelenskyy must therefore be portrayed in Moscow not as a fundamental shift in Serbia’s relationship with Russia, but as a response to Western pressure and Serbia’s own interests.
“Vucic is now trying to make sure that neither the West nor Russia becomes an open opponent during the election campaign,” said Vuksanovic.

“Zelenskyy was primarily received so that the ruling coalition could present itself to Europeans as a great friend of Ukraine. In the same way, Vucic is trying to present himself to the Trump administration as a great friend of Israel, primarily to ensure that neither the European Union nor the United States becomes an opponent of the ruling party during the election campaign,” he added.
Vucic’s room to maneuver is shrinking
The problem is that the room to maintain these relationships may be shrinking.
The deeper the confrontation between Russia and the West becomes, the harder it is for Serbia to remain close to both without facing pressure to choose.

The European Union increasingly expects candidate countries to align their foreign and security policies with those of the bloc. Serbia’s refusal to impose sanctions on Russia remains one of the most visible obstacles to closer alignment.

But Moscow, too, has reasons not to take Belgrade’s loyalty for granted, Vuksanovic said. He argued that Russia does not fully trust Vucic, even as Moscow continues to support his narrative about “color revolutions” — a reference to anti-government protests, in this case the student-led protests in Serbia that gathered pace in early 2025. Vucic and Russia have both portrayed the protests as Western-backed attempts to destabilize the government.

For Vucic, however, the longer-term question of Serbia’s ties with Russia can wait. The more immediate question is whether he will survive the election, tentatively scheduled for October, and remain in a position to preserve that delicate balance himself. /dl

articles.title: These Filipino films vie for a shot at Oscars 2027 success
articles.summary: This year's film shortlist features stories of social relevance, exploring themes of love, injustice, corruption, class division, and Philippine history from a different lens

items: The Philippines hopes to advance to the final list of Best International Feature Film nominees at the 99th Academy Awards next year, starting with eight films shortlisted by a National Selection Committee.

The shortlisted films reflect diverse aspects of the Filipino experience, addressing themes such as history, identity, and social issues, and each has the potential to resonate with international audiences.
A successful Oscars campaign could lead to increased tourism, economic growth, and enhanced confidence in the Philippine film industry.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The 99th Academy Awards are happening on March 14, 2027, and the Philippines wants in.

The country aims to take home its first-ever Best International Feature Film title at the prestigious cinema awards, and has started its bid by shortlisting eight films. These entries were handpicked by a National Selection Committee following a criteria of 50% artistic merit, 30% cultural relevance, and 20% capacity to campaign.

Put together by the Film Academy of the Philippines (FAP), the committee is composed of seven Filipino film practitioners who were pre-approved by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS).

“The films this year offer a spectrum of views of the Filipino experience. They look at our history, the issues we continue to face, and the ways Filipinos deal with questions of power, identity, love, freedom, and survival,” said FAP director-general Paolo Villaluna in a press statement.

“Each one has its own voice and approach, showcasing our cinematic merit and any of them has the potential to connect with audiences beyond the Philippines. Whichever film we send to the Oscars will carry a Filipino story that we can be proud of.”

If the Philippines is able to mount a successful Oscars campaign by earning a spot in the final shortlist, the country could potentially experience a boost in tourism, economic growth through increased local theater attendance, and bigger confidence in the film industry, among other benefits.

This new shortlist comes a year after the Philippines selected Lav Diaz’s Magellan for the 98th Academy Awards, a run that ended after the film fell short of advancing to the Academy’s official shortlist.
Here are the eight films contending to be the Philippines’ official entry to the 2027 Oscars:

blocks.caption: These Filipino films vie for a shot at Oscars 2027 success

blocks.text: 58th is an adult animated film that recounts the 2009 Maguindanao massacre carried out by the Ampatuan family ahead of the May 2010 elections. It claimed the lives of 58 individuals, most of which were journalists from different stations and outlets.

In 58th, director Carl Joseph Papa shifts things to a more personal level, as the events are retold from the perspective of Nenen, the daughter of photojournalist Reynaldo “Bebot” Momay, one of the 32 media personnel killed in the massacre. His body, however, was never found. Nenen, then, journeys toward seeking his official acknowledgement as a victim in the deadly 2009 event, and ultimately, finding justice for him.
Papa was also the director behind Iti Mapukpukaw, the Philippines’ official entry to the 2024 Oscars.

blocks.caption: These Filipino films vie for a shot at Oscars 2027 success

blocks.text: All The Things I Leave You (Patawid) is an Ilocano-language boys’ love (BL) film starring Benedix Ramos and Justin Basobas. It follows Jorge and Kiko, two young men who work at the same family-run restaurant in Ilocos. Along the way, the two work to decipher an old love story that had been left buried all these years, all while witnessing their own romance gradually unfold.

Directed by Jade Castro, the film made its international debut at New York’s NewFest, and was screened in India and Argentina. It was also named Best Episodic Film at the 37th Honolulu Rainbow Film Festival.

blocks.caption: These Filipino films vie for a shot at Oscars 2027 success

blocks.text: Directed by Rafael Manuel, Filipiñana’s story is told in the eyes of 17-year-old Isabel, who works as a tee-girl at an exclusive golf club in the Philippines, where she develops a fascination with its president, Dr. Palanca.
The black comedy film — which stars Jorrybell Agoto, Agot Isidro, Teroy Guzman, Shamaine Buencamino, Angeli Bayani, Ruby Ruiz, and Nour Hooshmand — offers a critique on the modern class divide.

Filipiñana had its world premiere in January at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Dramatic Special Jury Award for Creative Vision. It then debuted in Philippine cinemas in August as the closing film of the Cinemalaya Philippine Independent Film Festival.

blocks.caption: These Filipino films vie for a shot at Oscars 2027 success

blocks.text: Sigrid Andrea Bernardo’s I’mPerfect follows the romance of Jessica and Jiro (played by Krystel Go and Earl Amaba) — two individuals who have Down syndrome. The two lovers strive to live together independently despite circumstances making it difficult for them to achieve that.

The 2025 Metro Manila Film Festival (MMFF) Best Picture tells a tale of inclusion both on screen and in real life. It had taken Bernardo several attempts to find someone who was willing to produce the film, turning I’mPerfect into a full-blown movement championing individuals with down syndrome. Go, the film’s lead star, also won Best Actress.

blocks.caption: These Filipino films vie for a shot at Oscars 2027 success

blocks.text: Set in 1969 just before the declaration of Martial Law, Raymond Red’s Manila’s Finest sees Manila police district officer Homer Magtibay lead his team to address the rise of violent crime within the city. But when the Philippine Constabulary Metropolitan Command (MetroCom) starts to assert jurisdiction over specific cases, the effects of inter-service politics and corruption begin to seep into Homer’s life at home and at work.
The film — also an MMFF 2025 entry — stars Piolo Pascual, Jasmine Curtis-Smith, Cedrick Juan, Enrique Gil, Rico Blanco, Ashtine Olviga, and Ariel Rivera, among others.

blocks.caption: These Filipino films vie for a shot at Oscars 2027 success

blocks.text: Quezon is the third installment of director Jerrold Tarog’s “Bayaniverse,” a collection of films that spotlight key figures in Philippine history, such as Gregorio del Pilar in Goyo: Ang Batang Heneral, and Antonio Luna in Heneral Luna.

In Quezon, Jericho Rosales suits up to play Manuel L. Quezon, who was the first president of the Commonwealth of the Philippines. His presidential term lasted from 1935 to 1944. This film promises to portray the late leader as a human being and not as a hero.

blocks.caption: These Filipino films vie for a shot at Oscars 2027 success

blocks.text: In Silenced Nights, Andoy (played by Nico Antonio) suddenly finds himself bearing witness to the extrajudicial killing of a teenage boy in Manila. When he comes face to face with the boy’s mother, Marissa (played by Lotlot De Leon), he works to finally shed light on the truth.

The Lawrence Fajardo film received critical acclaim at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival, where it became the first-ever Filipino film to make it to the famed Canadian festival’s Platform Programme.

blocks.caption: These Filipino films vie for a shot at Oscars 2027 success

blocks.text: Sisa takes place in 1902 Philippines, at the tail-end of the American occupation. The titular character is a seemingly disturbed woman who finds herself in a concentration camp guarded by an American soldier. After appearing to be unable to remember her roots and even her name, she is eventually called Sisa, taking after the character in Jose Rizal’s Noli Me Tangere. It is later discovered that Sisa’s seemingly deranged disposition is all a front to hide her true identity as a spy to plot revenge against the Americans.
The Jun Robles Lana film marks veteran actress Hilda Koronel’s return to the screen after 13 years.

Sisa first premiered at the 2025 Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival in Estonia. It then went on to win Best Screenplay in the Director’s Week section of the 46th Fantasporto International Film Festival in Portugal. – Rappler.com

articles.title: WhatsApp chat used to send cash for crime and extremism
articles.summary: The WhatsApp money launderers arranged cash transfers in the UK and around the world with no paper trail.

blocks.text: A WhatsApp group chat was used to send hundreds of millions of euros in cash around the world, funding organised crime and extremism with no paper trail, an investigation by European broadcasters has found.
The 532-member group chat, called "Traders of Greater Europe", was used to arrange cash transfers across borders for their clients, including to British cities such as Birmingham and London.
In one case, payments from Brussels went to militants from the Islamic State group (IS) in Syria.

The European Broadcasting Union (EBU) investigative journalism network, which includes the BBC, also found wider evidence of similar cash transfer systems being used in people smuggling and drug trafficking.

The group chat, which contained more than 82,000 messages sent between late February and December 2022, was first uncovered by Belgian investigating magistrate Vincent Guerra. An investigating magistrate is a judge who examines evidence in complex cases before trial and makes a recommendation about whether they should proceed.

Guerra said the number of transactions was "staggering" and the network covered "the entire planet". The case began as an investigation into terror financing, but "it became just a drop in the ocean of transactions", he said.

Members of the group chat sent messages in Arabic to each other to set up cash payments using the ancient hawala transfer system. Hawala involves a network of trusted money brokers who can arrange for funds to be sent around the world without any electronic record or physical transport of bank notes.

The system involves an agreement between two brokers, known as hawaladars, in different locations. One of the hawaladars is paid a sum of cash and the other agrees to supply the same sum, minus commission, to the recipient. The hawaladars agree to settle up all their transactions between themselves at a later date.
Hawala transfers are frequently used for legitimate purposes, such as immigrant workers sending funds home to support their families in countries with limited access to banks.

But criminals can also take advantage of hawala transfers to avoid the Swift system used for most international money transfers, where banks typically flag large transactions outside the normal course of business and are required to report any suspicious activity.

The Great Traders of Europe group was reserved for transactions over €5,000 (£4,279) and payments were often much larger. There is no indication that all those participating in the group were involved in handling criminal funds.
Hawala is illegal in many countries, including most of the EU, but is legal in the UK as long as the brokers are registered with Revenue and Customs (HMRC).

The cache of WhatsApp messages was obtained by the EBU following a 2024 court case in Belgium which convicted six money launderers, including Abu Adam, the head of the network in Brussels, and his number two, Abu Ahmed.

Belgian police had discovered evidence that the defendants had been sending money to IS, which was intended to help the wives of militants escape from detention camps in Syria. When they arrested Abu Adam, they discovered the Traders of Greater Europe group chat on his phone.

Guerra said it was like "hitting the jackpot", uncovering the inner workings of a vast, underground system. The phone also contained 6,000 photos of €5 notes showing the serial numbers and 6,000 photos of identity cards. These details are often used as unique identifying codes in hawala transactions, and the total number of notes and ID cards suggest Abu Adam had processed at least 12,000 transactions, Guerra said.
"This isn't just amateur work; it's professional, and at a level we could never have imagined," he said. "They're bankers with no government oversight."

The EBU also found further gangs across Europe using the hawala system for criminal activity. One former money launderer previously involved in European hawala networks, whom we are calling Frank, told the EBU he had been involved in transactions totalling several hundred million euros.

His first introduction to the hawala system had been at an office in a small town outside Rotterdam, he said. There, five or six messengers had arrived with money in about an hour and a half, transferring at least a million euros, he estimated.

"What I found out later is that it's not just about money. It's about the financing of terror. It's about drug trafficking. It's about prostitution and all sorts of other crap, to put it nicely," he said.
Cases in Austria have also revealed how the hawala system is bound up with people smuggling and violence.

In one case investigated by Austrian broadcaster ORF, part of the EBU network, Austrian police raided what they called "the biggest hawala office in Vienna". It was run from a kebab restaurant on a busy thoroughfare and which authorities say was used to make payments for people smuggling.

Two Syrian brothers who ran the operation were charged with human trafficking, as well as torturing and raping a courier who had lost €350,000 (£300,000), saying he had been robbed. They were convicted last year and sentenced to 18 and 8 years in prison respectively.
Austrian police and Europol also recently dismantled another people-smuggling ring financed through hawala, which officials said had transported about 100,000 people into Europe over 18 months.

Gerald Tatzgern, who leads human-trafficking investigations at Austria's Criminal Intelligence Service, the BK, told ORF that torture was a reality of people smuggling and was also used to maximise profits.

He said: "Videos of the torture are then sent to the families, saying that if they don't send another €1,000 or several thousand euros, then the person concerned - your son, your brother, your father - will suffer."

articles.title: Tropical Depression Pilandok forms inside PAR, set to enhance habagat
articles.summary: No wind signals are up and landfall is unlikely, but PAGASA says it will continue enhancing the habagat.

blocks.text: Satellite image showing Tropical depression "Pilandok" as of 10:30 a.m. on Aug. 30, 2026.
PAGASA / Released
MANILA, Philippines — The low pressure area east of the country developed into Tropical Depression Pilandok on midday Sunday, August 30.
State weather bureau PAGASA said that Pilandok is expected to even enhance the persistent rains from the southwest monsoon, locally known as habagat.

As of 11 a.m, the tropical cyclone is estimated to be at 1,225 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon, packing maximum sustained winds of 45 kilometers per hour near the center and gustiness of up to 55 kph.
It was moving west-northwestward at 15 kph, with winds extending up to 420 kilometers from its center.
As of press time, no Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal was in effect.

PAGASA said Pilandok is unlikely to make landfall and is forecast to remain far from the Philippine landmass. The tropical depression is expected to move west-northwestward through Monday before turning northwestward to north-northwestward.
Pilandok is also forecast to be short-lived, remaining a tropical depression before weakening into a remnant low over the Philippine Sea south of Japan by Tuesday, September 1.
Habagat effects
While Pilandok poses no direct landfall threat, it is actively enhancing habagat, which is expected to bring heavy rainfall and severe winds to large parts of the country.
PAGASA forecasts strong to gale-force gusts caused by the enhanced monsoon expected to affect the following areas:

items: August 30: Most of Luzon and Visayas, alongside Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental
August 31: Most of the entire country
September 1: Most of Luzon and Visayas, as well as Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental

articles.title: Marikina conducts recovery ops amid bad weather
articles.summary: Despite the continuing inclement weather, the Marikina City government on Sunday, Aug. 30, began clearing and recovery operations in flood-affected areas following heavy rainfall brought by the…

blocks.text: Despite the continuing inclement weather, the Marikina City government on Sunday, Aug. 30, began clearing and recovery operations in flood-affected areas following heavy rainfall brought by the southwest monsoon (Habagat).

The Marikina City government deploys skid loaders, heavy equipment, and clearing personnel to quickly haul away garbage, mud, and debris left by the floods in Malanday and Tumana. (Photos from Marikina PIO)

blocks.caption: The Marikina City government deploys skid loaders, heavy equipment, and clearing personnel to quickly haul away garbage, mud, and debris left by the floods in Malanday and Tumana. (Photos from Marikina PIO)

blocks.text: It said that skid loaders, heavy equipment, and clearing personnel were deployed in Barangays Malanday, Tumana, Nangka, and Sto. Niño to quickly remove garbage, mud, and debris.
It added that cleanup operations will continue until the affected areas are fully cleared and cleaned up.

Marikina City Mayor Maan Teodoro said doctors are also making rounds at evacuation camps to provide doxycycline as protection against leptospirosis, particularly for residents who waded through floodwaters.
“Nagpabili na rin ako ng additional supplies pa para hindi tayo kulangin (I also ordered additional supplies so we won’t run short),” she added.

Teodoro, together with her husband, Rep. Marcy Teodoro, and rescue teams, personally monitored the weather conditions since Saturday, Aug. 29, to closely oversee the situation in the city and ensure the safety of residents.

blocks.caption: Marikina Mayor Maan Teodoro personally monitors the situation in the city amid flooding caused by heavy rainfall brought by the southwest monsoon (Habagat). (Photos from Mayor Maan Teodoro)

blocks.text: Marikina Mayor Maan Teodoro personally monitors the situation in the city amid flooding caused by heavy rainfall brought by the southwest monsoon (Habagat). (Photos from Mayor Maan Teodoro)

blocks.caption: Marikina Mayor Maan Teodoro personally monitors the situation in the city amid flooding caused by heavy rainfall brought by the southwest monsoon (Habagat). (Photos from Mayor Maan Teodoro)

blocks.text: Heavy rainfall on Saturday reportedly reached an average accumulated total of 136.6 millimeters from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. By 10:29 p.m., the Marikina River had reached the third alarm level after its water level rose to 18 meters, prompting the city government to implement forced evacuations, particularly in low-lying areas.
The third alarm level remained in effect until 3:30 a.m. on Sunday, with the river reaching a peak water level of 18.5 meters before gradually declining.
As of 1 p.m., the Marikina River had returned to normal, with its water level at 14.9 meters.

articles.title: Parañaque offers free doxycycline to residents exposed to floodwaters
articles.summary: Mayor Edwin Olivarez has directed health centers in all 16 barangays of Parañaque City to remain open on Sunday, August 30, to provide doxycycline prophylaxis to residents who waded through or walked…

blocks.text: A resident receives doxycycline prophylaxis at a health center in for possible leptospirosis exposure after wading through floodwaters (Photo from Parañaque PIO)

Mayor Edwin Olivarez has directed health centers in all 16 barangays of Parañaque City to remain open on Sunday, August 30, to provide doxycycline prophylaxis to residents who waded through or walked in floodwaters amid continued rains brought by the southwest monsoon, or habagat.
The city government said residents exposed to floodwaters may proceed to the nearest health center for proper assessment and guidance from health personnel on the appropriate use of doxycycline.

The preventive measure is intended to help reduce the risk of leptospirosis, a bacterial infection that may be contracted through exposure to water or soil contaminated with the urine of infected animals.
Olivarez urged residents to prioritize their safety and avoid walking or wading through floodwaters whenever possible, particularly when they have cuts or open wounds.
Residents who have been exposed to floodwaters and later develop symptoms such as fever, headache, muscle pain, or weakness were advised to seek immediate medical attention.
The city government continues to monitor the situation and provide health services to residents affected by the rains.
