articles.title: At least 37 dead and hundreds evacuated after strike on Kyiv weapons depot
articles.summary: An investigation has begun into the storage of weapons for Ukraine's military near a residential area.

blocks.text: Thirty-seven people have died and almost 400 have been evacuated after a Russian drone strike hit a depot storing weapons for Ukraine's military near a residential area on the outskirts of Kyiv.

The strike caused shells, mines and drones to detonate late on Friday, triggering a blast that damaged nearby properties including a care home for the elderly and disabled, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
He said the storage site "definitely shouldn't have been there" and that an investigation had been launched into "terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosive right next to people".
The attack is the second to hit a munitions depot near Kyiv in recent months, prompting renewed anger.
Four children are among the 42 people injured in Friday night's explosion, according to regional head Tymur Tkachenko, with a rescue operation ongoing at the site, in the Bucha district, on Saturday.

Russia's Ministry of Defence said in a statement that its forces had targeted "an ammunition depot" in Myla, a village to the west of the Ukrainian capital, holding "components and launch boosters for FP-1/FP-2 long-range unmanned aerial vehicles".
"Everything is completely damaged," local resident Liubov Pavlenko, 45, told the BBC after inspecting her home.
"There are cracks all around the entire perimeter, and cracks around the windows. Basically, the structural integrity has been compromised."
Zelensky said the decision to store explosives in the village was "absolutely unacceptable", adding: "Criminal proceedings have been opened on charges of official negligence."
The office of Ukraine's prosecutor general earlier said it was reviewing the "legality of the placement and storage of explosive objects and materials" near residential buildings in Myla.
It said the "actions of officials who made the relevant decisions" would also be investigated.
However, Zelensky earlier stated that "there are regulations in place - ammunition cannot be stored near homes or other residential areas", adding "appropriate conclusions will certainly be drawn".
He referenced the strike on an ammunition warehouse in Vyshneve in July, which caused a secondary detonation that killed nine, injured dozens more and damaged more than 280 homes.
Friday night's explosion has raised fresh questions about why munitions were being stored so close to people's homes, especially given the regularity of Russian aerial attacks.
"The authorities, the Ministry of Defence - why was this allowed at the depots, in a place where there used to be food?" Borys Daniyluk, 61, said.
"Why were ammunition and weapons stored there, next to a populated village? There are no words, just emotions."
Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky expressed regret that a "lesson" had not been learned following the explosion in Vyshneve.
The investigation into that incident revealed serious failings on the part of a state-owned company that had not complied with regulations regarding storage of explosives near residential buildings.
Zelensky indicated that the Myla depot had been operated by Ukraine's armed forces.
"In the fifth year of the full-scale invasion, making the same mistakes over and over is criminal negligence," Koretsky said on Telegram.
"Everyone responsible, without exception, must face severe punishment so that such situations never happen again."

Meanwhile, Tkachenko said a 14-year-old was killed in a separate attack in the Boryspil district, while Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said a two-year-old had died after a Russian drone crashed in Obolonskyi.

He added that five people, including an 18-year-old girl, were injured in fresh strikes on the capital on Saturday morning. Five people have been killed across the country over the past day, according to local officials.
Zelensky reported further overnight strikes in Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk, Sumy and Zaporizhzhia, as the Ukrainian army said it had shot down 233 Russian drones.
Russia and Ukraine have been intensifying their aerial attacks in recent months, with Kyiv focusing its operations on Russian economic targets.

Ukraine has for weeks struck sites belonging to Wildberries, the country's biggest online retailer, describing the firm as a legitimate target because it supplied components to the military, which Moscow denies.

articles.title: Royal Navy spent three days tracking Russian vessels in UK waters
articles.summary:
Three vessels and a helicopter deployed to monitor four ships travelling through the North Sea to the Channel

The Royal Navy spent three days tracking Russian vessels as they passed through…

blocks.text: The Royal Navy spent three days tracking Russian vessels as they passed through UK waters, it has emerged.
The “intense” 72-hour operation took place last week, with radars used to monitor four ships that made their way from the North Sea through to the Channel.
The fleet was surveilled by HMS Duncan, HMS St Albans and HMS Severn, with a Merlin helicopter providing support, officials said.
The Russian destroyer Admiral Levchenko was observed escorting the cargo vessels General Skobelev and Sparta, which are under sanctions, towards Dover.

In response, Russia deployed its own military resources, including the Neustrashimy frigate, to guard the shipment. Gen Gwyn Jenkins, the First Sea Lord, said there was “no room for complacency” as shadow fleet vessels continued to pose “an unacceptable risk” to UK security.

“Alongside our allies, this approach is forcing Moscow to divert Russian warships away from their core purpose,” he said. “That is because Russia knows we stand ready to act again, should it be required.”

The Royal Navy recently warned of increasing Russian activity in UK waters. In July, it spent 21 days monitoring ships from Moscow, an increase of 25% compared with the previous year. Officials say they have repeatedly observed warships in the Dover strait and the North Sea.
In June, the Royal Marines seized the Russian tanker Smyrtos, the first time British troops have directly boarded a shadow fleet vessel, one of more than 500 that have been sanctioned by the UK.

The Kremlin has threatened the UK after Andy Burnham visited Kyiv this week in his first overseas trip as prime minister. During the trip, Burnham said the UK would provide Ukraine with military support, including blueprints for components of long-range Scalp missiles.
after newsletter promotion

Although western officials have tried to play down the prospect of direct conflict between Russia and Nato, the Kremlin has accused the UK and its allies of “playing with fire” in relation to their continued support for Ukraine.

Andrei Fedorov, a former Russian foreign minister, said he could not “100% exclude” the possibility of “semi-military” action against Britain in retaliation, raising the prospect of an attack on British drone factories from “unknown sources”.

articles.title: Number of missing in Nepal and Tibet rises to nearly 3,000 as operations continue
articles.summary: Nepal requests foreign ⁠help in identification and storing of bodies, DNA testing and rescuing people from tunnels

blocks.text: The number of people killed in the floods in Nepal has risen to at least 675, the country’s disaster authority has said.

Seven have also been confirmed dead in Tibet by Chinese state media, taking the total killed when a glacial collapse unleashed a deadly torrent through river systems in the Himalayan mountains to 682.

Seven bodies have also been recovered in India from rivers flowing from Nepal and are believed to be flood victims. The number of people missing in Nepal and Tibet was revised up to nearly 3,000 on Saturday.

blocks.caption: People put up posters of missing family members at a hospital in Kathmandu, Nepal. Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: The missing list includes 517 foreigners and 933 workers on hydropower projects on the river where the torrent smashed down, Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.
A number of rescue workers are also missing, including 45 Nepali army soldiers and 40 police officers.
When a Chinese rescue team reached the all-but-obliterated Gyirong border crossing complex for the first time on Friday, they found “nothing but ruins”.
Surveillance camera footage from the complex showed huge torrents of water and debris on Wednesday engulfing buildings and people trying to flee. Only ⁠on Friday were rescuers able to reach the area.

blocks.caption: The glacier on Mount Langtang Lirung in Nepal, before and after its collapse. Composite: Planet Labs/AFP via Getty

blocks.text: Amid the deepening crisis, Nepal has now said it needs foreign ⁠help in specialised and technical areas, but not in search and rescue. On ⁠Friday, Nepal’s foreign ministry had said that Kathmandu could manage ​the rescue ​efforts on its own for ​now and declined foreign involvement.

The areas in which Nepal is seeking help include opening transport and communication services in places where bridges have been destroyed, identification of dead bodies, DNA testing, rescuing people stuck in tunnels, and storing bodies for longer durations, the foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, said late on Friday.

blocks.caption: People search lists for the names of relatives rescued from cut-off areas after the flash floods in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. Photograph: Dar Yasin/AP

blocks.text: Khanal said ​there was no ​need for assistance in general search and rescue which was being done by Nepali rescuers. “We think there is no need for repetition in this,” he said.
Nepal has requested that its neighbours, India and ​China, provide bailey bridges to reopen transport and communication in an area where about two dozen bridges have been destroyed.
So far, India has sent three flights carrying about 60 tons of relief material to Nepal, including blankets, medicines, food and water purification tablets, ⁠and a specialised tunnel rescue team.

blocks.caption: An aerial photo shows houses along the Trishuli River destroyed by the floods. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty

blocks.text: China has also dispatched five tunnel experts from Tibet to Nepal for flood-related rescue work, Chinese state media reported, as the country called for emergency aid to be sent to disaster-hit areas and for international rescue cooperation.

blocks.caption: Nepali army personnel rescue survivors from a hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa district, Nepal. Photograph: Nepal Army Handout/EPA

blocks.text: Rescuers – including army personnel and police – have been clawing through mud and using drilling equipment to reach more than 100 people trapped inside a hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa. More than 350 people have already been evacuated from the site under “extremely risky” conditions and the office of Nepal’s prime minister said the rescue effort had become “extremely challenging” due to adverse weather.
Search and rescue operations were temporarily halted because of rain and fog but resumed on Saturday afternoon after the weather improved.

Kawan Koirala, a rescue worker from the Nepal Scout Disaster Response Team, said they had been struggling in thick, leg-sucking mud. “People want their family member’s body back, either dead or alive, but we cannot find them … you can see the mud,” he told Agence France-Presse, exhausted after an 18-hour shift.
Nepal is continuing to monitor two barrier lakes upstream of the flood zone, with an official warning that flood risks will persist until both lakes fully drain.
Satellite imagery showed the second lake growing larger with no visible outlet, raising concerns that water pressure could still be building.

blocks.caption: A woman salvages usable materials from her house deluged in sludge after flash floods at Devighat in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. Photograph: AFP/Getty

blocks.text: China’s state-run Xinhua news agency said that the first barrier lake was reducing in size, citing analysis by the water resources ministry. A Chinese government geohazards expert warned, however, that the lake may be ‌unstable and that more than 100 glacial lakes scattered throughout the area could pose a threat.

In Beijing, a politburo meeting chaired by President Xi Jinping called for stronger monitoring of glacier lakes and landslide risks, and for closer international disaster cooperation, Xinhua reported.

China’s Premier Li Qiang, the country’s No 2 official, arrived in the area of Gyirong on Thursday afternoon, Xinhua said. The visit suggested Beijing was treating the disaster as a matter of ​the highest national priority.

In China, strict controls on the flow of information from one of its most sensitive regions are hampering the public’s understanding of events. The BBC and New York Times have reported that videos of the catastrophic floods, widely shared globally, have not appeared on Chinese social media sites.
Tibet, brought under Chinese control in the 1950s, is the most sensitive and tightly controlled region in the country.

blocks.caption: On the ground in Nepal after deadly flash floods – video

blocks.text: The Gyirong border port plays a key role in China’s belt and road network linking the country to south Asia, with logistics zones and vehicle parks built there in the past decade.
Nepal’s finance minister, Swarnim Waglé, estimated the country will ⁠need $4-$5bn (£3-£3.7bn) for rebuilding. “This is just an ​estimate. Loss and ⁠damage is ​being assessed,” he ​said.
More than 90,000 people have been affected by the disaster, the Red Cross estimated.
Some of the bodies being recovered had decomposed beyond recognition and will need to be identified using DNA samples, Nepali officials have said.

articles.title: Russian strike on ammunition depot near Kyiv kills dozens
articles.summary: Hundreds were also forced to flee after a Russian attack near Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, sparked a huge fire and explosions. The strike was the second to hit an arms depot near Kyiv in less than two…

image.caption: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country 'cannot be left alone in finding solutions to defend against' such drone strikesImage: Ukrainian Emergency Service/AFP

blocks.text: At least 37 people were killed after a Russian drone strike on a ammunition depot near Kyiv late Friday, one of the deadliest attacks in Ukraine this year.
The drone strike was the second attack to hit an arms depot near the Ukrainian capital in less than two months.
"A terrible situation and terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosives right next to people," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a video address on X.

"Another such crime — after what happened in Vyshneve — is absolutely unacceptable," he added. Zelenskyy was referring to an attack on an ammunition warehouse last month that set off secondary explosions in the small town on Kyiv's western outskirts, killing ten people.

Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified long-range strikes, increasingly hitting civilian infrastructure such as logistics warehouses and oil and port facilities. These attacks have resulted in more civilian casualties.
What else do we know about the Russian drone attack near Kyiv?

The strike sparked a major fire and explosions at the arms depot in the Bucha district, close to the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv, forcing more than 370 people to evacuate the region. Dozens were injured.

Among those killed was Taras Didych, head of the Dmytrivka community, who was one of the first to rush to the scene to rescue people, according to Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko. He also said the attack damaged at least 50 residential buildings.
Zelenskyy earlier said that criminal proceedings had been opened on charges of official negligence.
"There are regulations in place — ammunition cannot be stored near homes or other residential areas," Zelenskyy said.
Kyiv under jet-powered drone attacks
Friday's drone attack followed ​two days of constant air raids aimed at the Ukrainian capital and the surrounding region.

"Kyiv is under virtually nonstop attack from jet-powered drones. Ukraine cannot be left alone in finding solutions to defend against such strikes," said Zelenskyy, adding that Russia also struck nine other regions overnight.
It's been more than four and a half years since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of its neighbor.

articles.title: Jason Kidd takes in Filipino basketball passion at NBA House
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Jason Kidd was honored to experience a basketball-passionate country like the Philippines as he joined fellow NBA point guard Tony Parker and WNBA legend Lauren Jackson in the…

blocks.text: NBA legend Jason Kidd during his visit to Manila for the NBA House Philippines. –NBA PH PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines — Jason Kidd was honored to experience a basketball-passionate country like the Philippines as he joined fellow NBA point guard Tony Parker and WNBA legend Lauren Jackson in the launch of NBA House on Saturday at One Ayala in Makati.
Despite the inclement weather, Filipinos arrived at the opening of NBA House as early as 10 a.m. and stayed until the celebrity exhibition game coached by Kidd and Parker.

“The energy. The love of basketball, as much as we love it, you could see the Filipinos love the game of basketball and can play the game at a very high level so we’re very excited to be here,” said Kidd.

WATCH: Jason Kidd signs autographs and meets Filipino hoops fans during the opening of NBA House Philippines. | @LanceAgcaoilINQ pic.twitter.com/nrbvDK9YxE — INQUIRER Sports (@inquirersports) August 29, 2026
Parker and Jackson also took time to hold a brief basketball clinic for the young Filipino kids.
Filipino tennis ace Alex Eala and NBA champion Jordan Clarkson of the New York Knicks also gave a surprise video greeting to kick off the event.
“Hello NBA House Manila! I’m so excited to be in this guy’s presence (Clarkson),” said Eala. “Sending love back home.”
WATCH: Alex Eala and Jordan Clarkson greet the Filipino fans. | @LanceAgcaoilINQ pic.twitter.com/9u1FZKvJRy — INQUIRER Sports (@inquirersports) August 29, 2026

Kidd, a 10-time All-Star and second all-time in assists with 12,091, shared that his most memorable moments in the NBA were getting drafted, when he realized his dream of making it to the league, and winning a championship with the Dallas Mavericks.
Kidd and Dirk Nowitzki overcame the Miami Heat, featuring LeBron James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh, in the 2011 Finals.
The Hall of Famer attributed his success to Gary Payton, who became his mentor.

“If you have great teammates who want to score the ball, my job is easy. But I think being able to listen to the guys who played the game before me,” said Kidd. “So my mentor was Gary Payton, being able to listen to him, watch him because he played at the highest level, that was my dream was to be able to get to that level and so being able to have great people around me, I listened and then I tried to apply and I worked at it and I got lucky.”

After his storied career as a player, Kidd went into coaching, working with Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Milwaukee Bucks before winning the 2020 NBA bubble championship as an assistant coach with the Los Angeles Lakers, led by James and Anthony Davis.
His most recent coaching stint was with the Mavericks, where he steered Luka Doncic and Kyrie Irving to the 2024 NBA Finals before falling to the Boston Celtics.

articles.title: Public warned vs fake news as AFP bares foreign influence in VP trial
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution team has warned Filipinos against falling for fake news surrounding the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, amid an Armed Forces of the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution team has warned Filipinos against falling for fake news surrounding the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, amid an Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) disclosure that foreign malign influence operations are increasingly riding on local controversies, including the impeachment and flood-control issues.

Prosecution team adviser and spokesperson Robert Ace Barbers urged the public to scrutinize information circulating online and, whenever possible, go directly to the evidence being presented before the Senate impeachment court.

“Every day may fake news,” Barbers said, describing the steady stream of online narratives targeting members of Congress who endorsed the impeachment. He said that when critics cannot answer issues on substance, they resort to personally attacking those raising the questions.

His warning came after retired Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad, AFP spokesperson on the West Philippine Sea, said malign information operations have increasingly shifted from traditional pro-Davao and pro-China narratives to domestic controversies.
“Ngayon, mas mahirap ma-detect sapagkat impeachment sumasabay d’yan, Sanjia sumasabay d’yan, and other local issues; flood control sumasabay d’yan,” Trinidad said.
Trinidad said the pattern involves taking advantage of local issues and twisting narratives to favor China while attacking government officials who stand up on these issues.
He said such influence operations seek to shape public perception without the use of conventional military force.

AFP spokesperson Col. Francel Padilla said the military is monitoring developments in the information space and coordinating with other government agencies to determine the facts behind issues being circulated online.
Greatest weapon
“Our greatest weapon is the truth,” Padilla said, explaining that AFP intelligence and cyber units work together to establish facts and provide the public with information anchored on empirical data.

The two military officials also said the West Philippine Sea should unite Filipinos across political, regional, and religious lines as foreign malign influence operations expand from maritime disputes into domestic issues and social-media feeds.
For Barbers, the revelation makes it even more important for Filipinos to personally follow the impeachment proceedings and distinguish evidence from online narratives.

“Ang panawagan namin palagi sa ating mga kababayan, Kung maaari, subaybayan ninyo. Pakinggan ninyo at dinggin ninyo ’yung ebidensyang inilalatag. Nang sa ganu’n, ay maiwasan natin ’yung maniwala tayo sa fake news,” he said.
Barbers said the prosecution’s message is not to dismiss criticism or opposing views, but to ensure that the public has access to the facts and evidence needed to make its own judgment.
“Ebidensya ang dapat maging pakinggan,” Barbers said, stressing that the impeachment should not be reduced to a contest between personalities or political camps.
Barbers said the impeachment process is ultimately about accountability under the Constitution, not personalities or political camps.
“At the end of the day, ang mahalaga ho dito ay ang ating konstitusyon, ang ating saligang batas. Meron pong tinatawag na accountability mekanismo,” he said. /cb

articles.title: Ombudsman questions bail grants to graft convicts
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday questioned the granting of bail to some accused in graft cases before the Sandiganbayan, calling for convicted individuals to serve their jail terms more…

blocks.text: Published August 29, 2026 10:34pm

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday questioned the granting of bail to some accused in graft cases before the Sandiganbayan, calling for convicted individuals to serve their jail terms more swiftly.

“Sabi ko, marami naman ang nasisintensiyahan. Maraming nasisintensiyahan ang Sandiganbayan pero halos kaunti lang ang nakakulong. Paano? Sinasabi, meron daw tayong presumption of innocence at right to bail,” Remulla said on his radio program.
(Many are being sentenced. The Sandiganbayan sentences many, but only a few end up in jail. How is that? They say there is a presumption of innocence and a right to bail.)

“Pero ‘pag ika’y na-convict na sa lower court, convicted na sa Sandiganbayan, na-convict na ng RTC dito sa graft, dapat iyan kulong ka na. Ang problema, medyo sobrang bait ng korte at hindi ginagawa ‘yung trabaho na ipakulong ‘yung dapat ipinakukulong,” he added.

(But once you have been convicted by the lower court, by the Sandiganbayan, or by the RTC in a graft case, you should already be in jail. The problem is that the courts are being too lenient and are not doing their job of jailing those who should be imprisoned.)
Remulla proposed that bail be set at an amount commensurate with the damage caused by the accused.

“Grant sila nang grant ng bail. Ang bababa pa ng piyansa. Dapat kasi diyan, ‘pag na-convict na ‘yung tao at talagang may petition for bail, ang bail should be set, if ever kung iga-grant mo ‘yan, at the cost of damage na ginawa ng tao.”

(They keep granting bail, and the bail amounts are even low. If a person has been convicted and there is a petition for bail, the bail, if granted, should be set based on the cost of the damage caused by the person.)
Remulla added that bail should be paid through a cash bond rather than a bail bond.
The Ombudsman said his office had requested an inventory of individuals convicted by the Sandiganbayan, including whether they had served time in jail.
Remulla also criticized what he described as the apparent leniency of the judiciary when accused individuals file motions for reconsideration involving bail.

“Basta’t nagkaroon ng motion for reconsideration on a grant of bail, parang walang deadline ang judiciary… May rules sila na dapat sinusunod, hihingi sila permiso, ipapa-extend nila. Pero paano ‘yan, uupuan na lang nila forever? Umaabot ng 15 taon ‘yung kaso, nakaupo lang,” he said.

"Once a motion for reconsideration is filed against a grant of bail, it seems as though there is no deadline for the judiciary. They have rules that must be followed, but they ask for permission and seek extensions.
"What happens then? Are they just going to sit on the case forever? Some cases drag on for as long as 15 years without a resolution.)
GMA News Online has sought comment from the Sandiganbayan and will update this story once a response is received.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Death toll from Nepal-Tibet floods rises to over 600
articles.summary: Heavy rain is complicating an already difficult rescue effort, as hundreds remain missing three days after deadly flash floods hit the Nepal-Tibet border region.

image.caption: More than 2,400 people remain missing following the floods in NepalImage: Athit Perawongmetha/REUTERS

blocks.text: The latest death toll from the devastating flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border was reported on Saturday to be over 600, as frantic rescue operations to search for hundreds of missing people entered a fourth day.
Figures from both countries put the number of missing close to 3,000, with 682 bodies recovered and reports of corpses swept as far downstream as India.
According to Nepal's disaster agency, the death toll there now stands at 675, with 2,426 people — including foreigners — still missing.
Across the border in Tibet, China's state news agency, Xinhua, has confirmed seven deaths and reported 554 missing individuals.
A glacial collapse on Wednesday sent rock, ice, mud and debris surging through the Himalayan mountain river systems below.
The flood swept through areas near the Chinese border, ravaging entire towns and damaging hydropower plants.
What is the status of rescue efforts in Nepal?
Rainy weather conditions are hindering aerial rescue operations in Nepal.
Nepal army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet told the media on Saturday that helicopter operations were on hold until the weather improved.
Rescuers are battling thick layers of mud in the affected areas, which is making it difficult for helicopters to land and take off.
Tunnels in the mountainous region are also a challenge, Basnet said.
The army has located people trapped in a tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project in Nepal's Rasuwa District. Over 100 people are believed to be inside the tunnel filled with mud.

Basnet said that rescuers were struggling to locate the entry points of the tunnel and had made use of baskets and ropes to reach some people. There are also limited places for helicopters to land in the area.

blocks.caption: Members of the Nepal Army load relief material as a helicopter containing relief supplies takes offImage: Athit Perawongmetha/REUTERS

blocks.text: On Friday, Nepal's Army shared visuals of some people being rescued from the tunnel. The survivors were seen stuck in the mud, while officials crawled through the sludge and held out their hands to them.
On Saturday, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said a specialized tunnel rescue team had arrived from neighboring India and was ready to start work.
Nepalese authorities said the bodies of many flood victims have also been found dozens of kilometers from the disaster zone in Chitwan District in southern Nepal, which borders India.
Meanwhile, Indian authorities said they recovered the bodies of seven people who were swept downstream from Nepal and believe them to be flood victims.
More than 1,000 believed missing after Nepal flash floods
Nepal needs help in technical areas, says foreign minister
Late on Friday, Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the Reuters news agency that his country needed equipment, along with technical knowledge in tunnel rescue operations.

Khanal also told Reuters that Nepal did not need help with search and rescue operations but needed assistance in opening transport and communication lines in places where bridges were destroyed, identification of dead bodies, DNA testing and storage of bodies for a longer timeframe.
"We have already made requests for such ⁠specialized ​services and technical assistance in areas where we don't have enough expertise and technical know-how," ​Reuters quoted Khanal as saying.
Nepal's Foreign Ministry had on Friday declined foreign involvement in search and rescue.
Nepal's post-flood rebuilding estimated at $4-$5 billion
In another Reuters interview, Nepal's Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle said that the Himalayan nation may need $4 billion (€3.5 billion) ⁠to $5 billion ⁠to rebuild after the flood.
The estimate is equivalent ​to nearly a tenth of Nepal's economy.

"The initial estimate is ​between $4-$5 billion. Just an estimate," Wagle told Reuters, adding that the bill would be much less than what was needed in reconstruction after the disastrous 2015 earthquake — Nepal's worst ‌ recorded disaster.
"Loss and damage is being assessed," he said.

blocks.caption: People carry salvaged belongings from damaged houses following the flash floods and mudslideImage: Adnan Abidi/REUTERS

blocks.text: What do we know about rescue operations in Tibet?

In Gyirong, one of the hardest-hit areas in Tibet along the China-Nepal border, Beijing had temporarily halted its rescue efforts due to the risk of renewed flooding before announcing that the threat had waned.
China's Xinhua agency reported on Saturday morning that two villagers had been rescued in the Gyirong area.

blocks.caption: Rescue workers operate excavators and loaders to repair a damaged road leading to Gyirong PortImage: China Daily/REUTERS

blocks.text: The glacial collapse on Wednesday led to the formation of a barrier lake upstream due to debris dams. Experts warned that the lake had started to overflow.
On Saturday, Chinese authorities announced that the lake had begun to shrink.

China's state broadcaster, CCTV, cited the Ministry of Water Resources as saying that satellite imagery of the surface area of the lake in the Tsangpo River basin on Saturday morning showed a reduction of around 21,000 square meters compared to images from Thursday.
Authorities have also identified a larger body of water at the bottom of the glacier collapse.

"We estimate its area to be over 120,000 ⁠square ​meters, but its depth is currently unknown," Reuters quoted Chen Hongqi, a senior engineer at ​the Ministry of Natural Resources' Geological Disaster Technical Guidance Center, as saying.
Reuters also reported an official of Nepal's Disaster ​Management Authority as saying that flood risks will remain until the two lakes have fully drained.

articles.title: Lauren Jackson hails rise of women’s basketball, opportunities
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines —WNBA legend Lauren Jackson believes the continued rise of women’s basketball is giving young girls around the world more opportunities to turn their dreams into reality. Jackson,…

blocks.text: WNBA legend Lauren Jackson during his visit to Manila for the NBA House Philippines. –NBA PH PHOTO
MANILA, Philippines —WNBA legend Lauren Jackson believes the continued rise of women’s basketball is giving young girls around the world more opportunities to turn their dreams into reality.

Jackson, a three-time WNBA MVP and two-time champion with the Seattle Storm, relishes how the growing platforms for women’s basketball are putting the sport and its players in the spotlight like never before.

“Globally, women’s basketball is starting to take off. For me, working in the WNBL, WNBA, it’s nothing prouder. It could make me prouder of the women’s game,” Jackson said Saturday during the launch of NBA House at One Ayala in Makati.

“The platforms that the girls have now and people getting behind and putting their brands behind women’s basketball. You can see what it’s doing. It’s elevating the game and it’s putting women at the front and center.”

Jackson, who retired from the WNBL in 2024, also stressed the importance of having young athletes see professional players up close, whether in their national leagues or on the biggest stages such as the WNBA, with current-generation players Caitlin Clark, A’ja Wilson and Sabrina Ionescu taking the game to greater heights.

“I think it’s so important for young girls to be able to see those players playing in their national league, obviously watching the WNBA, the WNBL in Australia, but being able to see that their dreams are totally achievable,” she said.
“Making sure that the players get out into the community and work with the kids and mentor the kids. That’s the most important part.”
Jackson, a five-time Olympic medalist with Australia, is looking forward to the Fiba Women’s World Cup in Germany, now that women’s basketball has become a global phenomenon.
WATCH: WNBA legend Lauren Jackson is here at the NBA House. | @LanceAgcaoilINQ pic.twitter.com/Fqm5lCT8pQ — INQUIRER Sports (@inquirersports) August 29, 2026

“It’s going to be very exciting in Germany. Obviously we want the Opals to win a medal, but there are a lot of great teams. It’s going to be an interesting World Cup,” she said. “I think we’re going to see some new powerhouses in world basketball. Spain, France, China. I think China is going to be very good. We want a medal, obviously.”
The women’s basketball legend also enjoyed the chance to inspire young Filipino kids alongside NBA Hall of Famers Tony Parker and Jason Kidd.
“I was very fortunate to be a basketball player. I love the sport and for me it’s about being able to give back and being able to show these kids that anything is possible,” said Jackson.

“If we had opportunities like this when we were kids, it would have been amazing. I just think that the NBA does such an incredible job of getting out into communities and really exposing kids to basketball at an early age. It was very good,” she added.

“I think that any child that has a dream of playing in the NBA or the WNBA can do it. It requires a lot of hard work, but if they’ve got a dream and they’re willing to work for it, they can achieve it.”

articles.title: Number of missing in Nepal, China floods soars to nearly 3,000
articles.summary: NUWAKOT, Nepal — Rescuers in Nepal and China were still battling Saturday to locate thousands of people missing days after a deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayan…

blocks.text: NUWAKOT, Nepal — Rescuers in Nepal and China were still battling Saturday to locate thousands of people missing days after a deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayan region, engulfing villages.

The number of missing soared to nearly 3,000 Saturday, according to the latest figures from both countries, with 633 bodies recovered and reports that some of the dead may have been swept downstream as far away as India.

In an area home to vast energy infrastructure projects, Nepal’s disaster authority added 933 hydropower workers to a missing persons list that already included trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.
Those who made it out say they have lost everything and now face an agonizing wait to discover the fate of missing loved ones and the prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
“All the settlements near the river were swept away. There is nothing left,” survivor Buddhi Ram Dangol told AFP.
Samjhana Thing said she had been waiting three days for news of her missing brother.
“We don’t know anything. Hopefully he is in a safe place,” she said.
‘Enormous’ trauma
The trauma of Wednesday’s catastrophe has been “enormous,” and as many as 93,000 people may have been affected, the Red Cross said, with the death toll expected to rise.
Emergency teams had been racing to retrieve survivors from affected zones, where the widespread devastation meant food and water supplies were running out.
Compounding the search for the missing are fears of further flooding in affected areas.
The deluge of ice and mud caused huge lakes to form, and one of these formations has become a direct threat to emergency workers scouring the region for survivors.
Nepali police urged all rescuers to “immediately move to a safe location,” saying they had received information that “a water dam has burst again on the Tibetan side.”

In Tibet, where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, Beijing suspended its rescue operation in the hardest-hit area of Gyirong over the risk of renewed flooding before saying the threat had eased.
State news agency Xinhua reported early Saturday morning that two villagers had been rescued in the area.
‘All swept away’
On the Nepali side of the border, the military located people trapped in the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project, where they were working to find a way in to extract the survivors.
“Two helicopters have been dispatched, but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel,” army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP.
Some 350 workers and residents have been brought to safety from the site, he added, but efforts were ongoing to rescue more than 100 people trapped in the same area.
Workers rescued from other dam projects along the Trishuli valley described a disaster that unfolded with terrifying speed.
Buddha Tamang told AFP he survived only because he was inside a tunnel at the dam where he worked when the flood struck.
“The senior officers working on the other side, they were all swept away,” Tamang, who was airlifted on Thursday after being marooned for more than 24 hours, told AFP.
Nepal reported a death toll of 626 people on Saturday.
There are 2,426 people, including hundreds of foreigners, who are out of contact in Nepal.
Across the border in Tibet, which is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists, seven people died and 554 remain missing, state news agency Xinhua reported early Saturday.
Authorities also said they had evacuated 555 stranded tourists and 499 Chinese residents from Tibet.
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims.
Pilgrimage route
Scores of Hindu devotees from across the world are among those missing on the border, as many were on a pilgrimage to Tibet’s Mount Kailash.
Sivaranjani Muthunathan was traveling by bus with 56 others toward the Chinese border when they became stuck in what they thought was a traffic jam.
“Then there was fog, smoke, something that seemed to suddenly engulf us,” Muthunathan, 46, told AFP on Friday, showing a phone video she recorded of a torrent surging toward her.
Around them, vehicles were swept away or buried under mud.
“One by one, we also climbed out through the driver’s side,” then scrambled up a hill, she said. /das

articles.title: Ex-vice mayor Mangubat concedes Dasmariñas congressional race
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Former Dasmariñas Vice Mayor Raul Rex Rosario Mangubat on Saturday night conceded defeat to incumbent Mayor Jennifer “Jenny” Barzaga in the special congressional race for…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Former Dasmariñas Vice Mayor Raul Rex Rosario Mangubat on Saturday night conceded defeat to incumbent Mayor Jennifer “Jenny” Barzaga in the special congressional race for Cavite’s 4th District.

Mangubat conceded as partial and unofficial votes as of 8:30 p.m. showed Barzaga leading the congressional race at 185,668 votes—reflecting ballots from 41.50 percent of registered voters in the city.
The former vice mayor placed second, albeit by a significant margin, garnering only 23,208 votes so far.

“Tapos na ang halalan, at malinaw na ang naging pasya ng ating mga kababayan. Buong puso kong binabati si Jenny Barzaga. Ipinagkatiwala sa iyo ng mga Dasmarineño ang kanilang boto, pag-asa, at kinabukasan,” said Mangubat in a statement.

(The election is over, and the decision of our countrymen is clear. I wholeheartedly congratulate Jenny Barzaga. The people of Dasmarineños have entrusted you with their votes, their hopes, and their future.)
“Ang demokrasya ay hindi lamang tungkol sa ating karapatang pumili. Ito rin ay tungkol sa kababaang-loob na tanggapin at igalang ang pasya ng nakararami,” he added.
(Democracy is not just about our right to choose. It is also about the humility to accept and respect the decision of the majority.)
Mangubat then thanked his supporters, assuring them that their efforts were not wasted as they were able to prove that it was possible to lead an electoral campaign cleanly and honorably.

“Ngayong tapos na ang halalan, panahon na upang isantabi ang kulay at pagkakaiba. lisa lamang ang lungsod na ating mahal at iisa ang tagumpay na dapat nating hangarin ang pag-unlad ng bawat Dasmarineño,” he further said.
(Now that the elections are over, it’s time to put aside color and differences. There is only one city we love and one success we should strive for: the development of every Dasmarineño.)
Dasmariñas makes up the entire 4th District of Cavite, having 447,387 registered voters from 75 barangays.

Should Barzaga bag the Congressional seat, she will replace her son, Francisco “Kiko” Barzaga, who was expelled from his post by the House of Representatives last June 2 for “disruptive” and “disorderly” behavior.

This also effectively means the Barzagas’ hold on Dasmariñas as a political dynasty will continue, extending their political dominance in the city to nearly three decades since Elpidio “Pidi” Barzaga Jr. first became mayor in 1998. /cb

articles.title: Dinagat Islands residents protest Tubajon mining plan
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO, AGUSAN DEL SUR, Philippines — Residents of Barangay Navarro in Tubajon, Dinagat Islands, protested against a proposed mining project in their village, calling for greater protection of…

blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, AGUSAN DEL SUR, Philippines — Residents of Barangay Navarro in Tubajon, Dinagat Islands, protested against a proposed mining project in their village, calling for greater protection of local watersheds as the province grapples with a prolonged water crisis.

The protest was held outside the Navarro Barangay Hall on Aug. 27, where a meeting initiated by the Tubajon People’s Council was expected to bring together five barangay leaders, representatives of the proponent company and other officials to discuss how to manage the impact of the planned extractive operation.

Residents said they feared the plan could be endorsed without affected communities first being given enough opportunity to examine its contents. They raised concerns over the possible effects of mining on the Navarro and Imelda watersheds, nearby farms, coastal waters and fishing communities.
The meeting eventually did not push through.

Residents said their concerns had become more urgent because Dinagat Islands was already under a state of calamity due to a severe water shortage brought about by a prolonged dry spell. Around 18,000 people have been affected or placed at risk, while some communities have reportedly endured water shortages for about three months now.
They called for public consultations in all affected barangays, disclosure of the IMP and related documents, and protection of the remaining watersheds in Navarro and Imelda.

The Tubajon protest came as Dinagat Islands Rep. Kaka Bag-ao and Association of Philippine Electric Cooperatives party-list Rep. Sergio Dagooc, a Dinagat Islands resident, separately raised mining concerns involving Gibusong Island in the neighboring municipality of Loreto during a House budget hearing involving the Department of Environment and Natural Resources.

Both lawmakers urged the Mines and Geosciences Bureau to permanently trash the disputed mining applications in Loreto instead of merely suspending them, saying suspension could leave open the possibility that the applications may later be revived.
Bag-ao said the call for banning mining in the town was especially important because the province was already facing a severe water crisis affecting thousands of residents.

DENR officials committed to strengthen monitoring of mining activities in Dinagat Islands, visit Gibusong Island and meet affected communities, prevent mining in the Bonsai Forest in Mt. Redondo, and assign personnel to closely monitor mining areas.
The DENR also said Gibusong Island, which covers Barangays Helen, Liberty and Magsaysay in Loreto, could eventually be declared a “no-mining” area following proper assessment.
Residents in Navarro, meanwhile, vowed to continue monitoring developments and pressing government officials for transparency before any mining-related endorsement is made. /cb

articles.title: ‘Their whole village has disappeared’: frantic hunt for survivors in Kathmandu hospital
articles.summary: Family members pin photos of Nepal’s missing to hospital wall as people try not to give up hope on loved ones
articles.byline: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu

blocks.text: Posters of missing people line the wall of the hospital, the glue still fresh beneath. A schoolgirl smiling in her uniform; a beaming, chubby-cheeked baby; a couple smiling on their wedding day; a young man, hands on hips, atop a mountain peak; a young girl with flowing hair, peaking out from behind a door.

These faces are just a fraction of the thousands who have not been seen since deadly flash floods coursed through the Himalayas and wiped away entire villages. By Saturday morning, the toll of the missing had risen to almost 3,000, in both Nepal and Tibet.

blocks.caption: Relatives search through lists of people reported missing outside the hospital in Kathmandu. Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: So far, Nepal has recovered 669 bodies, but many remote areas have only been accessed by army helicopters on the hunt for survivors. Rescuers said it was too difficult to assess how many more people might be buried beneath the mud.
The task of identifying the dead is also gargantuan.
In the Nepali city of Chitwan, the morgues have been overrun by the sheer number of bodies and a makeshift building has been set up to house the dead.
Some of the bodies were carried so far down the river by the force of the floods, they were recovered in neighbouring India.

At Tribhuvan University teaching hospital in Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu, desperate relatives gathered in the hope of news. Four days on since the disaster struck, people continued to crowd round the police desk to register the names of missing family members. Hundreds of the injured are recovering in the hospital’s wards and people were frantically checking lists of patients, desperate to find a sign that their loved ones were still alive.

blocks.caption: Relatives look through the lists of missing flood victims at the teaching hospital. Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: In the absence of information and with affected areas almost completely cut off, many families have resorted to making posters to appeal for information. Yavraj Lama said his sister, her husband and their two children were missing after their village of Jaydada, in Rusawa district, had been entirely washed away.
His eyes filled with tears as he glued a photo of one-year-old Sijan Tawang, a baby in the arms of his mother, to the hospital wall. A picture of 12-year-old Sahil, his brother, hung next to it.

“We are numb, we don’t have words to say how sad and distraught we are,” said Lama. “Our main focus is trying to find baby Sijan. He was so sweet and innocent; it’s impossible for us to think he is not with us any more.
“But their whole village has disappeared,” he added, “so we have no hope left that any of them survived.”

blocks.caption: Monita Nepali, right, whose husband is missing, is comforted at the hospital in Kathmandu. Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: Monita Nepali, 22, howled in grief as a poster of her missing husband, Vishal Nepali, 30, was pinned to the hospital wall. They had married six months ago and his work as a driver regularly took him to the border between Nepal and Tibet. She had spoken to her husband an hour before the floods hit when he was out for a morning walk in Rusawa. He had promised to call her that evening, but his phone has been ever off since.

“I don’t want to live on the face of this earth without him,” she said. Four days may have passed, Nepali said, but she had not stopped believing in her husband’s return. “I feel it in my heart he will come back.”

For some families, the scale of the loss was too hard to comprehend. Tulmaya Tamang, 36, came to the hospital bearing posters of some of her 12 family members, including her five-month-old niece, who lived in a village in Rusawa and have not been seen since the floods.
“Our family is under tremendous stress,” she said. “So many are gone, and those of us who are left behind are struggling.”

As hopes for their survival faded, Tamang said they were now just hoping the bodies could be retrieved. “If we had the bodies, then at least we could have peace,” she said. “Otherwise, the family will never stop wondering and this pain will go on for a very long time.”

At least 900 of those still missing were working on the vast hydropower projects along the Trishuli River corridor, high up in the Himalayas, which were decimated by the floods and mudslides. Many of the workers were low-paid labourers, including at least 63 from India.

blocks.caption: A Nepali soldier rescues a survivor from a hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa district, Nepal. Photograph: Nepal Army Handout/EPA

blocks.text: On Friday, dramatic footage showed Nepali soldiers pulling several survivors out through a thick wall of mud from a tunnel in the Trishuli-1 hydropower project. The Nepali army said they believed at least another 100 people were still trapped inside the tunnels, as well as dozens more stuck underground in the Trishuli-3 hydropower plant.

Among those missing was 24-year-old Sujan Nepali, who had just finished his night shift at the hydropower project and was asleep in bed when the wall of water came gushing down the valley. At the hospital trauma centre in Nepal, his sister, Sushisha Maluwar, had returned anxiously every day to check if his name was listed.

“We haven’t lost hope,” she said. “We are writing down his name at the hospitals and putting up his photographs everywhere, hoping that we might find him somewhere. Maybe he has already been rescued. Maybe he had managed to escape and survive.”

MANILA, Philippines–Carl Tamayo is out for Sunday’s Fiba World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers game against Iran due to a sprained ankle he sustained during Gilas Pilipinas’ overtime win over Jordan.
The Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas made the announcement late Saturday, with coach Tim Cone to replace Tamayo with Justin Arana, the newest member of the Gilas pool.
It appears that Gilas deemed Tamayo’s ankle too swollen for him to play in the crucial fixture at Mall of Asia Arena.
Tamayo rolled his ankle during the third quarter of the contest on Friday, resulting in a bad fall. The Korean Basketball League mainstay was able to walk back under his own power.
However, Tamayo spent the rest of the game on the bench as Gilas went on to take an 82-81 victory after a five-minute overtime period.

Cone opted for Arana over RJ Abarrientos, who is also part of the pool for the fourth window.

articles.title: Baricuatro hails Halad sa Pagtuo 2026: ‘Very successful’
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Cebu Gov. Pamela Baricuatro hailed the province’s inaugural Halad sa Pagtuo as “very successful,” as thousands gathered for a celebration centered on faith, local culture,…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Cebu Gov. Pamela Baricuatro hailed the province’s inaugural Halad sa Pagtuo as “very successful,” as thousands gathered for a celebration centered on faith, local culture, and community participation.

The celebration, one of the highlights of Cebu Province’s 457th founding anniversary, brought together 50 local government units (LGUs) for a carroza procession and seven festival contingents for cultural presentations.
“Everybody said that it was a good idea presenting all our carrozas. So I’m very happy, and I’m very excited,” Baricuatro told reporters.
The procession began at the Capitol grounds near 3 p.m. before the festivities continued at the Cebu City Sports Center with a Holy Mass, blessing of carrozas, and festival presentations.
Higher subsidies for LGUs

In a previous interview, Executive Chief of Staff James Canoy said the provincial government allocated up to ₱19 million for the celebration, covering LGU subsidies, carroza preparations, and other expenses.
Under the new format, each of the seven LGUs chosen for the festival presentations received ₱2 million, while every LGU that joined the carroza procession received ₱100,000 for preparations.

The seven contingents were Sinulog sa Carmen, Tuba Festival of Borbon, Bisnok Festival of Dumanjug, La Torta Festival of Argao, Hinulawan Festival of Toledo City, Dagitab Festival of the City of Naga, and Kabkaban Festival of Carcar City.
The presentations were not structured as a competition, making Halad sa Pagtuo a scaled-down version of the province’s previous Pasigarbo sa Sugbo celebration.
Provincial tourism head Rowena Montecillo earlier said the celebration was renamed Halad sa Pagtuo upon Baricuatro’s request to highlight Cebu’s local faith traditions.
Fewer contingents possible

Baricuatro said consultations with LGUs are still needed to determine whether future editions will become a competition, with the possibility of limiting participation to one representative per district.
“Siguro we keep it like seven lang, or one per district, para ‘di kayo dugay (We can keep it at seven participants in total, or one per district, so the program won’t run long),” the governor said.
Alcantara, Daanbantayan, and Cordova were unable to join the procession because their local fiestas conflicted with the celebration.
The other localities across the province, including Cebu’s highly urbanized cities, participated in the festivities.
Thousands attend
Baricuatro said the celebration demonstrated Cebu’s potential to draw large crowds by bringing together local governments, provincial officials, Capitol employees, and the general public.
“This is really it — a new festival is born in Cebu!,” Baricuatro said.
As of 7 p.m., Cebu City Police Office director Ricky Sumalde estimated that roughly 7,000 people were at the venue.
The program ended around 8:30 p.m. with a special performance by Filipino artist Martin Nievera.

articles.title: Leptospirosis cases in PH hit 5.5K in first 8 months of 2026
articles.summary: MANILA – The Philippines recorded 5,486 leptospirosis cases nationwide from Ja. 4 to Aug. 26, 2026, a 23 percent decline from the 7,163 cases reported during same period last year, the…

blocks.text: MANILA – The Philippines recorded 5,486 leptospirosis cases nationwide from Ja. 4 to Aug. 26, 2026, a 23 percent decline from the 7,163 cases reported during same period last year, the Department of Health (DOH) said Friday.
DOH Undersecretary Gloria Balboa said the National Capital Region (NCR), Cagayan Valley and Central Luzon recorded the highest cumulative numbers of leptospirosis cases nationwide.

“Dito sa NCR po, binabantayan natin yung mga areas na nakikita natin may mas mataas na kaso. At sa itong nakita natin itong Aug. 27 as of yesterday po, 521 na ang pasyente na naitala dito sa Metro Manila (Here in NCR, we are monitoring the areas where we see higher cases. And as of yesterday, Aug. 27, we recorded 521 patients here in Metro Manila),” Balboa said during a press briefing at the National Kidney and Transplant Institute in Quezon City on Friday.
She noted that 158 of the total NCR patients were admitted at the San Lazaro Hospital.
Surge in hospitalizations is expected over the next two weeks due to the incubation period of the leptospira bacteria.
To manage the expected influx of patients, the DOH activated dedicated leptospirosis fast lanes across 33 DOH-retained hospitals in affected regions.
The agency also established inter-hospital referral networks to prevent overcrowding at tertiary specialty centers.

Under this mechanism, specialized institutions like the National Kidney and Transplant Institute and the Philippine General Hospital will coordinate step-down care for recovering patients to free up high-level ICU equipment and dialysis units for severe cases.
DOH Assistant Secretary Lester Tan urged those who waded through floodwaters to seek medical evaluation within 24 to 48 hours, whether they have open wounds or visible symptoms.

“Ang maagang diagnosis at treatment sa loob po ng dalawang araw mula na magsimula ang mga sintomas ay makakatulong po upang maiwasan ang mga komplikasyon ng sakit at ang pagkaka-ospital (Early diagnosis and treatment within two days from the onset of symptoms will help prevent complications of the disease and hospitalization),” he said.
Tan emphasized that untreated leptospirosis could result in kidney failure, liver damage, meningitis, or multi-organ failure.

The DOH assured the public that government health centers, LGU facilities and DOH hospitals maintain an adequate supply of post-exposure prophylactic antibiotics, such as doxycycline, which must be taken under a physician’s prescription. (PNA)

articles.title: F1: Lando Norris extends McLaren stay until 2030
articles.summary: LONDON–Reigning F1 world champion Lando Norris has committed his long-term future to McLaren after signing a contract extension that will keep him at the team until 2030. The new deal comes less than…

blocks.text: McLaren driver Lando Norris of Britain lifts the trophy after winning the Formula One Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort , Netherlands, Sunday, Aug. 23, 2026. (AP Photo/Darko Bandic)
LONDON–Reigning F1 world champion Lando Norris has committed his long-term future to McLaren after signing a contract extension that will keep him at the team until 2030.
The new deal comes less than a week after Norris secured back-to-back wins with victory at the Dutch Grand Prix, rekindling the British driver’s hopes of a successful defence of his world title.
It includes an option for a multi-year extension beyond 2030, McLaren said in its announcement on Saturday.
Last season, the 26-year-old Norris delivered McLaren’s first drivers’ title since Lewis Hamilton won it in 2008.
Norris joined McLaren’s junior program when he was just 17 and made his F1 debut two years later, in 2019.
“McLaren is my home, and I’m very pleased to be signing a new contract to keep me with the team until at least 2030,” Norris said in a team statement.
“When I started this journey nine years ago, I was clear about the goals I wanted to achieve: to get McLaren back to the front and to win championships.
“We’ve achieved that goal, but we want more, we want to keep on winning, and we know as a team that we’re capable of achieving it.”
Norris sits fourth in this year’s championship, trailing Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli by 83 points with 11 races left in the season.
His McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri extended his contract at the start of the 2025 season on a deal that is believed to run until at least 2028.

McLaren won constructors’ titles in 2024 and 2025, ending a championship drought that had stretched back to 1998, but the team was well off the pace at the start of this season after struggling to master the new rules.
Norris’s resurgence has shown there is still all to play for after wins in Hungary and the Netherlands with an improved car.
“Lando has been an integral part of McLaren’s journey and success over the last nine years, and we are delighted to continue our partnership with him,” said team principal Andrea Stella.

“He is an exceptional driver, someone who combines outstanding natural speed with maturity, consistency and a strong commitment to McLaren, but above all, he is a special human being who is valued by everyone in the team.”
Stella added: “With him and Oscar, we know we can count not only on one of the strongest partnerships but also on one of the most united and close-knit teams in Formula 1.”
Norris will also receive one of the MCL39 cars that he used to secure his first F1 title last year as a gift from the team.

articles.title: Prosecution panel not ruling out Lachica as witness in Sara Duterte impeachment trial
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel is not ruling out the possibility of presenting former Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSPG) commander Colonel Raymund Lachica as a witness in the…

blocks.text: Published August 29, 2026 9:30pm

The House prosecution panel is not ruling out the possibility of presenting former Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSPG) commander Colonel Raymund Lachica as a witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, according to former Surigao del Norte congressman Robert Ace Barbers.

Barbers, the designated adviser to the House prosecution panel, said they have yet to call Lachica to testify in connection with the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) alleged misuse of confidential funds because they do not need his testimony yet.

“Hindi sarado ang aming isipan para ipresenta si Colonel Lachica. Kung naniniwala kami na mayroong kakulangan o kinakailangan pang madagdagan ang evidentiary value or puwedeng sumuporta sa aming allegations, bakit hindi?” Barbers said on Saturday.
(Our minds are not closed to presenting Colonel Lachica. If we believe there is a gap, or we need to add evidentiary value or support our allegations, why not?)
Asked whether the prosecution was concerned that Lachica might take full responsibility for the alleged misuse of the funds, Barbers said they were prepared for such a possibility.

“Kung sakaling 'yan ang kanyang gagawin, it doesn't give us any evidentiary value doon sa allegations namin. Problema niya 'yun. Kung 'yun ang gagawin niya, siya 'yung mananagot sa batas,” Barbers said.
(If he does that, it doesn't give us any evidentiary value for our allegations. That is his problem. If that is what he does, he will be held accountable under the law.)
The defense also listed Lachica as a witness, so the prosecution is prepared to cross-examine him if he takes the stand, Barbers said.
During the August 17 hearing, former OVP Special Disbursing Officer Gina Acosta said that Duterte was the one who asked her to disburse P125 million in confidential funds to Lachica.
On August 25, Lachica expressed his readiness to appear before the Senate impeachment court “to tell the truth, subject to applicable laws and security restrictions.”
Barbers said the prosecution will present four more witnesses in the coming trial days: three officials from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and defense counsel Michael Poa.
Poa is set to be designated as a hostile witness. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Tony Parker believes Wembanyama, Spurs are close to NBA glory
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — San Antonio Spurs legend Tony Parker sees a bright future in the Victor Wembanyama era, believing the franchise could win it all sooner rather than later. A four-time NBA…

blocks.text: San Antonio Spurs legend Tony Parker during his visit to Manila for the NBA House Philippines. –NBA PH PHOTO
MANILA, Philippines — San Antonio Spurs legend Tony Parker sees a bright future in the Victor Wembanyama era, believing the franchise could win it all sooner rather than later.
A four-time NBA champion and former Finals MVP, Parker is confident that Wembanyama and the Spurs can bring glory back to San Antonio after losing to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals last June.
“The potential is amazing. You know, I think it’s just a matter of time before they win the championship,” said Parker on Saturday during the launch of the NBA House at One Ayala in Makati.

WATCH: Tony Parker talks about his visit in the Philippines and the future of San Antonio Spurs with Victor Wembanyama. | @LanceAgcaoilINQ pic.twitter.com/fSB6fL1lCi — INQUIRER Sports (@inquirersports) August 29, 2026
The six-time NBA All-Star won championships in 2003, 2005, 2007 and 2014 with Tim Duncan and Manu Ginobili under coach Gregg Popovich.
Parker also had a storied international career with the France national basketball team, where Wembanyama also plays. France settled for silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics after losing to Team USA.
Like what he sees from the Spurs, the legendary point guard also believes Wembanyama can take France to greater heights.

blocks.caption: Victor Wembanyama Spurs vs Knicks Game 5 NBA Finals

blocks.text: San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama sits on the floor after a foul during the second half of Game 5 of the NBA Finals basketball series against the New York Knicks, Saturday, June 13, 2026, in San Antonio. (AP Photo/Ross D. Franklin)
“Same thing. I hope we get a lot of gold medals. I think we have a very, very good team. And now we just have to keep working hard,” he said.

The 44-year-old Parker has been enjoying his time in Manila, holding a basketball clinic for Filipino kids with WNBA legend Lauren Jackson on Saturday. He also coached celebrities against Jason Kidd in an exhibition game.

“I love it.. Every time I can share my experience and spend some time with the kids, I think it’s priceless. And I used to love it when I was that age. I always loved spending time with professional basketball players,” said Parker.
WATCH: Tony Parker is here to hold a basketball clinic for Filipino kids with Lauren Jackson. | @LanceAgcaoilINQ pic.twitter.com/sbcnKduMB2 — INQUIRER Sports (@inquirersports) August 29, 2026
“And I’m happy to be here. You can see the passion, the energy is amazing. And we know, you know, in the Philippines, they love the NBA.”
“Since I arrived the love here is amazing. And so, I love everything.”
Parker also stressed the importance of fundamentals to kids aspiring to become professional basketball players.

“I think that’s the basics, You have to start from there. So, that’s why those camps are very important. Every exercise we did today is the foundation, how you’re going to become a good player, a great player, if you want to go all the way to the NBA,” Parker said.

articles.title: Lachica testimony not needed to prove VP misused confidential funds – Barbers
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – The House impeachment team does not need Col. Raymund Dante Lachica’s testimony to establish its allegation that Vice President Sara Z. Duterte misused confidential…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The House impeachment team does not need Col. Raymund Dante Lachica’s testimony to establish its allegation that Vice President Sara Z. Duterte misused confidential funds, its adviser and spokesperson Ace Barbers said Saturday.
Barbers said evidence already presented before the impeachment court was sufficient to establish Duterte’s role as the head of the agency and approving authority over the confidential funds.

“Hindi namin kailangan iyong kanyang testimonya para makapagbigay-lakas o diin dito sa aming allegation,” Barbers said, referring to Lachica, during the Saturday News Forum at Dapo Restaurant in Quezon City.

Lachica, former security chief of the Office of the Vice President (OVP), figured prominently in the testimony of two hostile witnesses presented by the prosecution—former OVP special disbursing officer (SDO) Gina Acosta and Assistant Secretary and Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio.

Acosta testified that she turned over four P125-million tranches of OVP confidential funds to Lachica upon Duterte’s instruction even though he was not the SDO or fidelity-bonded accountable officer for the money.

She also testified that she did not personally witness how the money was distributed and relied on reports and assurances from Lachica in preparing the liquidation documents for which she remained the accountable officer.
Ortonio, meanwhile, testified that Duterte approved the confidential fund disbursement vouchers and liquidation reports.
He also confirmed that only the vice president, as head of agency, and Lachica, as her chief security officer, had personal knowledge of how the confidential funds were actually implemented.

Barbers said the prosecution believes these testimonies, together with those of Land Bank of the Philippines officials and Commission on Audit auditors, already support its allegations under Article I pertaining to Duterte’s misused of confidential funds.

He dismissed the possibility that prosecutors were holding back from calling Lachica out of concern that the security officer could take responsibility for the transactions and shield Duterte from accountability.
“Anuman ang sasabihin niya na maaaring maka-turn around o maka-turn ng aming presentation ng ebidensya, sa aming paniwala, it will not matter. It will not matter,” Barbers said.

“Kasi matibay na at sufficient na sa ngayon, sa puntong ito, na itong mga witnesses na pinresenta namin ay nakapagbigay-lakas at magbibigay ng diin doon sa aming allegations of misuse, misappropriation, at of course, itong sinasabi nating irregular liquidation,” he added.
Barbers also rejected suggestions that the prosecution is afraid to put Lachica on the witness stand.
“Ba’t naman matatakot sa kanya?” he said.
He recalled that the House Committee on Good Government and Public Accountability repeatedly summoned Lachica during its 2024 inquiry into Duterte’s confidential funds, but he did not appear.
“Eh unang-una, tinatawag namin siya noon sa Committee on Good Government. Hindi naman siya humarap. Ilang beses siya pinatawag, hindi rin siya humarap,” Barbers said.
Barbers noted that the prosecution has already presented hostile witnesses who worked closely with Duterte.

“So hindi kami dapat matakot because tatlo na nga iyong hostile witness na pinresenta natin, mas malalapit ito sa ating Pangalawang Pangulo, di ba? At kailangan pa ba kami magdagdag ng pang-apat? Sa aking paniwala, hindi,” he said.

The prosecution is expected to next present Duterte defense lawyer and former Department of Education undersecretary and chief of staff Michael Wesley Poa. It plans to ask the impeachment court to declare him its third hostile witness.
As for Lachica, Barbers said the prosecution sees no need to call him at this point but is keeping the option open should his testimony later become necessary.

articles.title: LTFRB summons 21 bus, UV Express operators for various violations
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines—The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) on Saturday said it has summoned 21 operators of buses and UV express units for violating the rules at the Edsa…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) on Saturday said it has summoned 21 operators of buses and UV express units for violating the rules at the Edsa Busway as well as operating dilapidated units.
In a statement, the agency said show cause orders were issued to bus operators following the deployment of “mystery riders.”

The “mystery riders” were tasked with monitoring bus drivers who deliberately slow down their buses, with the LTFRB noting that traffic enforcers have been directed to implement a 30-second rule in bus stops.
It added that two drivers and a bus conductor were also apprehended along Edsa Busway for smoking inside the vehicle.

Show cause orders were also issued to several operators of UV Express services over their use of “dilapidated and smelly” vehicles following complaints from passengers, with the majority of the vehicles were apprehended along routes in Bulacan going to Metro Manila
The LTFRB said their violations included having a non-functioning air conditioner, faded paints, a “dilapidated” chair and an “unpleasant” smell inside the vehicle.
All the operators who received the summons were asked to explain why their franchise should not be revoked or suspended amid their violations.

Amid the issuance of show cause orders, acting LTFRB chairperson Greg Pua Jr. urged operators of public utility vehicles (PUVs) to follow the rules and regulations that were established to ensure a safe and comfortable transportation.
“There are conditions that PUV operators are mandated to comply with—all of them are anchored on road safety and professionalism of the country’s public land transportation system,” he said.
“Accountability comes for those who chose to defy or ignore these conditions, and this is what the LTFRB did in the case of these 21 bus and UV Express operators,” added Pua. /gsg

Chinese state media earlier confirmed seven dead in Tibet following Wednesday’s disaster, taking the total killed to 682.
The number of missing in Nepal remained constant at 2,426, after a sharp hike in numbers on Saturday morning.

That missing list includes 517 foreigners, as well as 933 workers on hydropower projects on the river where the torrent smashed down, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
The number of missing also includes 45 Nepali Army soldiers, 40 police officers, and 19 immigration and customs officers.
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims. However, they are not included in the toll.

articles.title: Niger's defense ministry says soldiers attempted mutiny
articles.summary: Gunfire and explosions were heard across Niamey overnight. The attack posed the latest threat to Niger's military junta, led by Abdourahamane Tchiani, who seized power in a 2023 coup.
articles.byline: Emmy Sasipornkarn, Dharvi Vaid Dhulia, Zac Crellin

image.caption: The main airport in Niamey was reportedly targeted by the attacks [FILE: August 8, 2026]Image: Sam Mednick/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Niger's Ministry of National Defense ‌on ⁠Saturday said ⁠that ​a group of soldiers shot at "sensitive" locations in the capital Niamey in an apparent mutiny.
Gunfire and explosions had been heard across Niger's capital, Niamey, overnight into the early hours of Saturday morning.
Attackers had targeted Diori Hamani International Airport, which also houses a military air base, and attempted to breach the security perimeter around ​the presidency.
"Another cowardly attack on Base 101 and once again our defense and security forces ensured ... Situation under control," said lawmaker Bana Wagana Ibrahim, who serves on the Consultative Council.
Niger military 'gradually regaining control'
The military said it was "gradually regaining control" after mutineers took soldiers hostage at a base near the airport in Niamey, AFP news agency reported.
Authorities urged the public to "remain calm and freely go about their business" in a statement read out on public television and signed by Defense Minister General Salifou Mody.
The attack posed the latest threat to Niger's military junta, led by Abdourahamane Tchiani, who seized power in a 2023 coup.
Niger, like its Sahelian neighbors Mali and Burkina Faso, has for years been ruled by a military junta that has struggled to stem a jihadi insurgency.
National TV signal reportedly cut after gunfire
The shooting began around 1 a.m. local time (0000 GMT) and continued until daybreak.
Locals said that the country's national television had gone off air.
Tele Sahel's satellite and online programming was replaced with a black screen at 9 a.m. local time (0800 GMT), AFP reported. It was restored around one hour later.

Niamey has been targeted by jihadists twice this year: once by the so-called "Islamic State in the Sahel" group (EIS) and again in June by their rivals from the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM).

articles.title: DOLE orders contractor of collapsed Pampanga building to pay P11.49M in wages, fines
articles.summary: The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) on Saturday said the contractor behind the collapsed building in Angeles City, Pampanga is liable for P11.49 million in unpaid wages and administrative…

blocks.text: Published August 29, 2026 8:14pm

The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) on Saturday said the contractor behind the collapsed building in Angeles City, Pampanga is liable for P11.49 million in unpaid wages and administrative fines.

In a statement, the DOLE said Golden Years Construction and Steelworks Corporation and building owner Ernest Jackson Lim failed to pay workers’ benefits and committed occupational safety and health (OSH) violations even before the building collapsed.

“The amount includes P1.17 million in unpaid wages during the Work Stoppage Order (WSO), underpaid wages, unpaid rest day premiums and holiday pay, as well as P10.32 million in administrative fines for OSH violations,” the DOLE said.
The decision stemmed from a resolution signed by DOLE Secretary Francis Tolentino on August 17.
The DOLE said the workers’ claims were meritorious, including their entitlement to rest day premiums during the implementation of the work stoppage order from October 16 to 24, 2025.

“A review of the records established several serious OSH violations, including failure to provide personal protective equipment, secure required permits for mechanical lifting equipment, deploy required safety officers and first aiders, and provide temporary accommodation for workers,” the agency said.
The DOLE also found that fake and invalid certificates had been submitted for the project’s first aider and safety officer.
The respondents were ordered to pay the monetary award and administrative fines within 10 days of receiving the resolution.
The nine-story building under construction collapsed before dawn on May 24, killing 30 people. —VBL, GMA News
